title: 2004 Ukrainian presidential election
summary: The 2004 Ukrainian presidential election was a pivotal event [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s political history, marked by widespread allegations of fraud and the subsequent Orange Revolution. The election culminated in a Supreme Court ruling that invalidated the initial results, leading to a re-run that resulted in Viktor Yushchenko's victory over Viktor Yanukovych.

title: 2006 Ukrainian parliamentary election
summary: The 2006 Ukrainian parliamentary election, held on 26 March 2006, marked a significant political event [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], following the constitutional amendments that transformed the country's governance structure. This election was characterized by a party-list proportional representation system and resulted in a coalition government formation amidst political turmoil.

title: 2007 Ukrainian parliamentary election
summary: The 2007 Ukrainian parliamentary election took place on 30 September 2007, following a political crisis that led to the dissolution of the Verkhovna Rada. The election resulted in a narrow majority for the Yulia Tymoshenko Bloc and Our Ukraine-People's Self Defence, while the Party of Regions entered opposition.

title: 2010 Ukrainian presidential election
summary: The 2010 Ukrainian presidential election was a significant political event in Ukraine, taking place on 17 January 2010, followed by a run-off on 7 February. Viktor Yanukovych emerged as the President-elect, marking a pivotal moment in Ukraine's political landscape.

title: 2012 Ukrainian parliamentary election
summary: The 2012 parliamentary election [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], held on 28 October, marked a significant political event characterized by a mixed electoral system and the emergence of new political parties. This election was notable for being the last in which Crimea participated before its annexation by Russia in 2014.

title: 2015 Ukrainian local elections
summary: The 2015 Ukrainian local elections, held on 25 October, marked a significant political event [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], occurring amid ongoing conflict and territorial disputes. A second round of mayoral elections took place on 15 November 2015 in cities where no candidate achieved a majority.

title: 2019 Ukrainian parliamentary election
summary: The 2019 Ukrainian parliamentary election, held on 21 July 2019, marked a significant political shift in Ukraine, resulting in President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's Servant of the People party achieving an outright majority. This election was characterized by a high turnover of elected officials, with a substantial number of newcomers entering parliament.

title: 2019 Ukrainian presidential election
summary: The 2019 Ukrainian presidential election, held on 31 March, resulted in a runoff on 21 April between Volodymyr Zelenskyy and incumbent president Petro Poroshenko, with Zelenskyy winning decisively. This election marked a significant political shift in Ukraine, as Poroshenko became the third incumbent president to lose reelection.

title: 2020 Ukrainian local elections
summary: The 2020 Ukrainian local elections, held on 25 October 2020, involved the election of deputies to district councils, rural townships, and city mayors, with a significant impact on local governance [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]. title: 2022 Kharkiv counteroffensive
summary: The 2022 Kharkiv counteroffensive was a significant military operation conducted by the Armed Forces of Ukraine against Russian forces during the [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|Russo-Ukrainian war]], commencing on 6 September 2022. This counteroffensive led to the rapid recapture of key territories in Kharkiv Oblast, demonstrating Ukraine's military capabilities and impacting the overall dynamics of the conflict.

title: 2022 Kherson counteroffensive
summary: The 2022 Kherson counteroffensive was a significant military operation launched by Ukraine on 29 August 2022, aimed at reclaiming territories occupied by Russian forces in the southern regions of Kherson and Mykolaiv oblasts. This counteroffensive marked a pivotal phase in the ongoing conflict, leading to the liberation of Kherson, the only regional capital captured by Russia since the invasion began.

title: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine

title: Battle of Ilovaisk

title: Battle of Kiev

title: Battle of Kruty

summary: The Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine is the highest executive authority in the country, responsible for implementing state policies and governing various ministries. Established on April 18, 1991, it has undergone several structural changes and is currently led by Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi since July 16, 2026.

title: Carpathians
summary: The Carpathian Mountains, known as Карпати in Ukrainian, are a significant mountain range in Central and Southeast Europe, extending approximately 1,500 km (930 mi) and featuring diverse ecosystems and geological formations. The range plays a crucial role in Ukraine's natural landscape and biodiversity.

title: Category:Steel industry in Ukraine
summary: The steel industry is a crucial component of Ukraine's economy, being the country's leading heavy industry and a significant player in global iron and steel production. In 2007, Ukraine ranked as the eighth largest producer and third largest exporter of iron and steel worldwide.

title: Catholic Church in Ukraine
summary: The Catholic Church in Ukraine, comprising various rites including the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church and the Latin Church, plays a significant role in the religious landscape of the country. Approximately 13-14% of Ukraine's population identifies as Catholic, with a majority belonging to the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church.

title: Central Election Commission of Ukraine
summary: The Central Election Commission of Ukraine (TsVK) is an independent body responsible for organizing and conducting presidential, parliamentary, and local elections in Ukraine, as well as managing referendums. Established in November 1997, it operates under the Constitution and laws of Ukraine, ensuring the electoral process's legality and transparency.

title: Central Rada
summary: The Central Rada, also known as the Central Council, was a significant governing body in the Ukrainian People's Republic that played a crucial role in the national movement for Ukrainian independence from 1917 to 1918. It was established as a revolutionary parliament and aimed to lead [[ukraine|Ukraine]] towards full sovereignty.

title: Centrenergo
summary: Centrenergo is a significant electric and thermal energy producer in central and eastern [[ukraine|Ukraine]], contributing approximately 8% to the country's electricity production and about 18% to thermal generation. The company plays a crucial role in maintaining Ukraine's energy balance.

title: Chechen–Russian conflict
summary: The Chechen–Russian conflict is a prolonged ethnic and political struggle between Chechen forces and various Russian governments, including the Imperial, Soviet, and modern Russian states. This conflict has historical roots dating back to the 18th century and has significant implications for regional stability, including impacts on Ukraine through ongoing armed groups.

title: Cherkasy
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Cherkasy is a city of regional significance located in central Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Cherkasy Oblast and Cherkasy Raion. With a population of 269,836 as of 2022, it has historical roots dating back to the 13th century and has played a significant role in Ukraine's cultural and political history.

title: Cherkasy Oblast
summary: Cherkasy Oblast, also known as Cherkashchyna, is a province in central [[ukraine|Ukraine]] situated along the Dnieper River. It serves as an important agricultural and administrative region, with a population of approximately 1,160,744 as of 2022.

title: Chernihiv
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Chernihiv is a city and municipality located in northern Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of [[chernihiv-oblast|Chernihiv Oblast]] and Chernihiv Raion. With a population of 282,747 as of 2022, Chernihiv has a rich historical significance, having been an important cultural and political center since the 9th century.

title: Chernihiv Oblast
summary: Chernihiv Oblast is a province located in northern Ukraine, with its administrative center in the city of Chernihiv. As of 2022, the oblast has a population of approximately 959,315 and encompasses an area of around 31,900 km².

title: Chernivtsi
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Chernivtsi is a city of regional significance in southwestern Ukraine, located on the upper course of the Prut River. Historically the capital of Bukovina, the city has played a vital role in the cultural and administrative landscape of Ukraine.

title: Chernivtsi Oblast
summary: Chernivtsi Oblast is a province in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], encompassing parts of the historical regions of Bukovina and Bessarabia. It is the smallest oblast in Ukraine by both area and population, with a diverse geography and a complex historical background.

title: Chernivtsi University
summary: Yuriy Fedkovych Chernivtsi National University is a prominent public university located in Chernivtsi, [[western-ukraine|Western Ukraine]]. Established in 1875, it has a rich history tied to the region's cultural and educational development, and it is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Chernobyl
summary: Chernobyl, or Chornobyl, is a partially abandoned city located within the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone in Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine. It gained international notoriety following the catastrophic nuclear disaster in 1986, leading to the evacuation of its residents and the establishment of a restricted area due to radioactive contamination.

title: Chernobyl disaster
summary: The Chernobyl disaster, which occurred on April 26, 1986, at reactor 4 of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant near Pripyat, Ukraine, is one of the most catastrophic nuclear accidents in history. It resulted in immediate fatalities and long-term health issues, marking a significant event in Ukraine's history and impacting nuclear safety worldwide.

title: Chernobyl Exclusion Zone
summary: The Chernobyl Exclusion Zone, also known as the 30-Kilometre Zone, is an administrative territorial entity [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] established after the 1986 [[chernobyl-disaster|Chernobyl disaster]]. It encompasses approximately 2,600 km² and remains one of the most radioactive areas in the world, with significant implications for public health, environmental monitoring, and historical memory in Ukraine.
aliases: Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant Zone of Alienation

title: Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant
summary: The Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant (ChNPP) is a decommissioning nuclear power facility located in northern Ukraine, near the city of [[pripyat|Pripyat]]. It is historically significant due to the catastrophic disaster that occurred in 1986, which has had lasting impacts on nuclear safety and environmental policy [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] and beyond.
aliases: Vladimir Ilyich Lenin Nuclear Power Plant

title: Chervona Ruta
summary: Chervona Ruta, or 'Red Rue', refers to both a mythological flower and an actual plant species significant in Ukrainian culture. The legend surrounding this flower is intertwined with Ukrainian traditions and has inspired various cultural expressions, including music and festivals.

title: Chervonohryhorivka
summary: Chervonohryhorivka is a rural settlement located in the Nikopol Raion of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine, with a population of 6,030 as of 2022. It serves as the administrative center for the Chervonohryhorivka settlement hromada.

title: Chop
summary: Chop refers to various subjects, including a city in Ukraine, medical terms, and cultural references. The term is notably associated with the city of Chop, which plays a significant role in the region's geography and transport.

title: Chornomornaftogaz
summary: Chornomornaftogaz is a Ukrainian oil and gas enterprise focused on natural gas extraction in the Black Sea region, established in 1978. It operates as a subsidiary of Naftogaz and has faced significant challenges since the [[russian-annexation-of-crimea|annexation of Crimea]] in 2014.

title: Chortkiv
summary: Chortkiv is a city located in Chortkiv Raion of [[ternopil-oblast|Ternopil Oblast]], [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of the raion. With a population of approximately 28,279 as of 2022, Chortkiv has historical significance and is known for its architectural monuments and cultural heritage.

title: Chuhuiv
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Chuhuiv is a city of regional significance located in Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Chuhuiv Raion. As of February 2024, the city has a population exceeding 30,000 residents and is known for its military history and educational institutions.

title: Chumak
summary: Chumak was a historical wagon-based trading occupation in Ukraine during the late Medieval and early Modern periods, characterized by the long-distance transport of goods using oxen-drawn carts. This occupation played a significant role in the trade of various commodities, particularly salt, and influenced Ukrainian culture and folklore.

title: Chyhyryn
summary: Chyhyryn is a city located in [[cherkasy|Cherkasy]] Raion, [[cherkasy-oblast|Cherkasy Oblast]], central Ukraine, situated along the Tiasmyn River. Historically significant as the residence of the hetman of the Zaporizhian Host and the capital of the Cossack Hetmanate, Chyhyryn has played a crucial role in Ukraine's political and cultural history.

title: Chyhyryn Raion
summary: Chyhyryn Raion was a district in Cherkasy Oblast, central Ukraine, known for its historical significance during the Ukrainian War of Independence. It was dissolved in 2020 as part of administrative reforms in Ukraine.

title: cinema of Ukraine
summary: Ukrainian cinema encompasses the creation and production of films within Ukraine and by Ukrainian filmmakers internationally. The industry has a rich history marked by significant contributions and challenges related to national identity and external influences.

title: civic nationalism
summary: Civic nationalism, also referred to as democratic nationalism, is a political ideology that emphasizes liberal values such as freedom, tolerance, and equality, distinguishing itself from ethnocentric forms of nationalism. This ideology is particularly relevant in the context of Ukraine, where national identity plays a crucial role in shaping civic engagement and democratic governance.

title: Clairette blanche
summary: Clairette blanche is a white wine grape variety primarily cultivated in France, particularly in regions such as Provence, Rhône, and Languedoc. Its relevance extends to Ukraine through the exploration of diverse grape varieties for winemaking.

title: coal in Ukraine
summary: The coal industry has played a significant role in Ukraine's economy and energy sector, particularly in the eastern regions. Historically, Ukraine has been a major coal producer in Europe, with substantial reserves primarily located in the Donets basin.

title: Coat of arms of Ukrainiae
summary: The coat of arms of Ukraine, known as the tryzub, features a blue shield with a golden trident and serves as a significant national symbol. Officially adopted on 19 February 1992, it reflects Ukraine's historical and cultural heritage.

title: Constitution of Ukraine
summary: The Constitution of Ukraine, adopted on 28 June 1996, serves as the fundamental law of Ukraine, establishing the framework for the country's governance and legal system. It is significant for its role in defining the rights of citizens and the structure of the [[cabinet-of-ministers-of-ukraine|Ukrainian government]].

title: Constitutional Court of Ukraine
summary: The Constitutional Court of Ukraine is the highest judicial authority responsible for interpreting the [[constitution-of-ukraine|Constitution of Ukraine]] and ensuring the constitutionality of laws and legal acts. Established on 18 October 1996, the Court plays a crucial role in the Ukrainian legal system, with its decisions being binding and final.

title: Cossack Hetmanate
type: vassal and tributary state of the Ottoman Empire
summary: The Cossack Hetmanate, officially known as the Zaporozhian Host, was a stratocratic state established by Registered [[cossacks|Cossacks]] in [[dnieper-ukraine|Dnieper Ukraine]], existing from 1648 to 1764. It played a significant role in [[history-of-ukraine|Ukrainian history]], particularly through its interactions with the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and the Tsardom of Moscow.

title: Cossack Mamay
summary: Cossack Mamay, or Kozak Mamai, is a prominent folklore hero [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], symbolizing the spirit and culture of the [[cossacks|Cossacks]]. His image has been widely represented in various forms of Ukrainian art and literature, especially following the dissolution of the Zaporozhian Sich in 1775.

title: Cossack raids
summary: Cossack raids were a series of military offensives conducted by the Zaporozhian Cossacks of southern [[ukraine|Ukraine]] and the Don Cossacks of southern Russia from 1441 to 1774, primarily targeting the Crimean Khanate, the Nogai Horde, and the Ottoman Empire. These raids were a response to the Crimean–Nogai slave raids and involved actions such as freeing enslaved Christians and plundering settlements.

title: Cossack song
summary: Cossack songs are a genre of folk music that originated among the Cossacks of Ukraine, particularly during the 16th and 17th centuries. These songs reflect the historical and cultural experiences of the Cossack community, emphasizing themes of heroism, separation, and the bond with horses.

title: Cossackia
summary: Cossackia refers to the traditional regions inhabited by Cossack communities in Russia and Ukraine, particularly associated with the Zaporizhian Host. The term has also been used to propose an independent Cossack state, particularly during the early 20th century and World War II.

title: Cossacks
summary: The Cossacks are a significant social class in [[history-of-ukraine|Ukrainian history]], primarily composed of East Slavic, Eastern Orthodox Christian individuals who originated from the Pontic–Caspian steppe. They played a crucial role in military defense and the development of the southern [[administrative-territorial-entity-of-ukraine|regions of Ukraine]] and surrounding areas.

title: Council of Europe
summary: The Council of Europe (CoE) is an intergovernmental organization founded in 1949, dedicated to promoting human rights, democracy, and the rule of law across Europe. With 46 member states, including Ukraine, the CoE plays a vital role in fostering cooperation and safeguarding fundamental freedoms.

title: Crimea
summary: Crimea is a peninsula located in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]], bordered by the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, and is internationally recognized as part of Ukraine. The region has a complex history marked by various cultures and powers, and has been under Russian occupation since 2014.

title: Crimea crisis
summary: The Crimea crisis encompasses significant historical and contemporary events related to the region of Crimea, particularly its conflicts and geopolitical implications for Ukraine. Key events include the Crimean War and the ongoing Russian occupation and [[russian-annexation-of-crimea|annexation of Crimea]], which are critical to understanding Ukraine's territorial integrity and national sovereignty.

title: Crimea – Gold and Secrets of the Black Sea
summary: The exhibition 'Crimea – Gold and Secrets of the Black Sea,' also known as 'Scythian Gold,' is a significant cultural showcase that highlights the historical artifacts of Ukraine, particularly those from Crimea. It was held in Germany and the Netherlands from 2013 to 2014 and became embroiled in legal disputes following the Russian annexation of Crimea.

Crimea – The Golden Island in the Black Sea

title: Crimean Khanate
summary: The Crimean Khanate was a [[crimean-tatar|Crimean Tatar]] state that existed from 1441 until its annexation by the Russian Empire in 1783. It played a significant role in the [[history-of-ukraine|history of Ukraine]], particularly in the context of the region's ethnic and political dynamics.

title: Crimean Tatar
summary: Crimean Tatar refers to both an ethnic group and a language associated with the Crimean Tatars, who are a significant minority [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], particularly in the [[crimea|Crimean Peninsula]].

title: Crimean Tatar culture
summary: Crimean Tatar culture represents the heritage of the indigenous Turkic people of Ukraine, primarily established on the [[crimea|Crimean peninsula]]. This culture has evolved significantly since the era of the Crimean Khanate, which lasted from 1441 to 1783, and remains deeply intertwined with the history and traditions of Ukraine.

title: Crimean Tatars
summary: Crimean Tatars are an Eastern European Turkic ethnic group indigenous to Crimea, with a rich history shaped by various migrations and cultural influences. Their population and cultural identity have faced significant challenges, particularly during the Russian Empire and the Soviet Union, yet they remain a vital part of [[ukraine|Ukraine]]'s demographic and cultural landscape.

title: Crimean War
summary: The Crimean War was a significant conflict fought from October 1853 to February 1856 between Russia and an alliance of the Ottoman Empire, France, the United Kingdom, and Sardinia. Its implications extended to Ukraine, particularly through the involvement of the Black Sea region and the geopolitical dynamics that shaped the area during this period.

title: Cucuteni–Trypillia culture
summary: The Cucuteni–Trypillia culture is a Neolithic–Chalcolithic archaeological culture that thrived from approximately 5050 to 2950 BC in Southeast Europe, particularly in regions of modern-day Ukraine. It is notable for its large settlements, advanced agricultural practices, and significant contributions to early urban development.

title: culture of Ukraine
summary: The culture of Ukraine encompasses the material and spiritual values of its people, shaped by a rich history that includes strong family ties, religious influences, and traditional arts. This culture has persisted through various historical challenges and has seen a revival since Ukraine's independence in 1991.

title: Cyborgs: Heroes Never Die
summary: Cyborgs: Heroes Never Die is a 2017 Ukrainian war drama film that depicts the experiences of Ukrainian defenders during the Second Battle of Donetsk Airport amidst the ongoing conflict in [[donbas|Donbas]]. The film, which highlights themes of courage and patriotism, was both a critical and commercial success [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

title: Dakh Daughters
summary: Dakh Daughters is a [[music-of-ukraine|Ukrainian music]] and theatre ensemble formed in 2012 in Kyiv, known for its unique blend of musical styles and cultural influences. The group, consisting of seven women, engages with themes of heritage and identity through their performances and lyrics.

title: dance in Ukraine
summary: Ukrainian dance encompasses the traditional folk dances of the Ukrainian ethnic group and those from various other ethnic groups within Ukraine. It includes household folk dances, folk-stage dances, and notable genres such as circle dances and thematic story dances, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of Ukraine.

title: Daniel of Galicia
summary: Daniel of Galicia (1201–1266) was a significant ruler in Ukrainian history, serving as Prince of Galicia and Volhynia, Grand Prince of Kiev, and King of Ruthenia. His reign marked the restoration of the Romanovichi dynasty's power and the establishment of the Kingdom of Galicia–Volhynia, making him a pivotal figure in the region's political landscape during the Mongol invasions.

title: Danylo Halytsky Lviv National Medical University
summary: Danylo Halytsky Lviv National Medical University (LNMU) is one of the oldest and largest medical institutions in Ukraine, tracing its origins back to 1784. Named after King [[daniel-of-galicia|Daniel of Galicia]], the university has played a significant role in the development of medical [[education-in-ukraine|education in Ukraine]].

title: Daria Kaleniuk
summary: Daria Kaleniuk is a prominent Ukrainian civil society activist and the executive director of the Anti-Corruption Action Center in [[kyiv|Kyiv]], known for her advocacy against corruption and her efforts to gain international support for Ukraine during the 2022 Russian invasion.

title: decentralisation in Ukraine
summary: Decentralisation in Ukraine refers to a series of reforms aimed at enhancing the powers and resources of local authorities, promoting regional development and administrative efficiency. Initiated after Ukraine's independence, these reforms gained momentum following the Euromaidan protests in 2014, with significant support from international organizations.

title: Declaration of Independence of Ukraine
summary: The Act of Declaration of Independence of Ukraine was adopted by the Supreme Soviet of the [[ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic|Ukrainian SSR]] on 24 August 1991, marking the reestablishment of Ukraine's state independence from the Soviet Union. This declaration was confirmed by a referendum on 1 December 1991, leading to widespread international recognition and the eventual dissolution of the Soviet Union.
aliases: Act of Declaration of Independence of Ukraine

title: decommunization in Ukraine
summary: Decommunization in Ukraine refers to the process of removing communist symbols, monuments, and names from public spaces, which began in the early 1990s and intensified after the 2014 Revolution of Dignity and the onset of the Russo-Ukrainian War. This movement aimed to reject totalitarian ideologies and reshape the national identity of Ukraine.

title: Defenders of Ukraine Day
summary: Defenders of Ukraine Day is a public holiday in Ukraine observed on October 1, honoring veterans and fallen members of the Ukrainian armed forces. The holiday was first celebrated in 2015 and has its roots in the historical traditions of honoring military defenders.

title: Denys Shmyhal
summary: Denys Anatoliiovych Shmyhal, born on 15 October 1975, is a prominent [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] politician and entrepreneur who served as the 18th Prime Minister of Ukraine from 2020 to 2025. His political career includes significant roles in managing Ukraine's response to the COVID-19 pandemic and the defense during the 2022 Russian invasion.

title: deportation of the Crimean Tatars
summary: The deportation of the Crimean Tatars, known as Sürgünlik, occurred from May 18 to 20, 1944, when at least 191,044 individuals were forcibly displaced by Soviet authorities under Joseph Stalin's orders. This event is a significant chapter [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s history, highlighting the ethnic cleansing and cultural genocide faced by the Crimean Tatar community.

title: Derkach
summary: Derkach is a Ukrainian surname that translates to 'ratchet' or 'noisemaker.' It is associated with several notable individuals, primarily from [[ukraine|Ukraine]], across various fields such as politics, sports, and music.

title: divisions of the Carpathians
summary: The Carpathians are a significant mountain range in Ukraine, categorized into various divisions that highlight their geological and geographical complexity. This categorization includes major provinces and subdivisions, reflecting the diverse landscapes and cultural influences across the region.

title: Dmitri Shostakovich
summary: Dmitri Dmitriyevich Shostakovich was a prominent Soviet-era composer and pianist, born on 25 September 1906 in Saint Petersburg. His complex relationship with the Soviet government and his significant contributions to music, including symphonies and operas, have established him as a key figure in the cultural [[history-of-ukraine|history of Ukraine]] and the broader Soviet Union.

title: Dmytro Bortnianskyi
summary: Dmytro Bortniansky (28 October 1751 – 10 October 1825) was a prominent composer of Ukrainian Cossack descent, recognized for his significant contributions to the musical heritage of both Ukraine and Russia. He served as a harpsichordist and conductor at the court of Catherine the Great and is celebrated for his liturgical works and choral concertos.

title: Dmytro Hnatyuk
summary: Dmytro Mykhailovych Hnatyuk (28 March 1925 – 29 April 2016) was a prominent Soviet and Ukrainian baritone opera singer and a former member of the Ukrainian Parliament, recognized for his significant contributions to the arts [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

title: Dmytro Kuleba
summary: Dmytro Kuleba is a prominent [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] politician and diplomat who served as Minister of Foreign Affairs from March 2020 until September 2024. His extensive career in Ukraine's foreign service and his active role during critical periods in the country's history highlight his significance in shaping Ukraine's international relations.

title: Dmytro Pavlychko
summary: Dmytro Vasylyovych Pavlychko was a prominent Ukrainian poet, translator, scriptwriter, culturologist, and politician, whose contributions significantly influenced [[ukrainian-literature|Ukrainian literature]] and statehood. He played a vital role in the political landscape of Ukraine during its transition from Soviet rule to independence.

title: Dmytro Razumkov
summary: Dmytro Oleksandrovych Razumkov is a prominent Ukrainian politician who served as the Chairman of the Verkhovna Rada from August 2019 until October 2021 and was the leader of the Servant of the People party. His political career has significantly influenced Ukraine's legislative landscape, particularly during the 2019 parliamentary elections.

title: Dmytro Yarosh
summary: Dmytro Anatoliiovych Yarosh is a Ukrainian activist, politician, and military commander known for his leadership in the Right Sector and the Ukrainian Volunteer Army. His political career includes serving as a People's Deputy of Ukraine and founding the Governmental Initiative of Yarosh, reflecting his significant influence in contemporary Ukrainian politics.

title: Dmytro Yavornytsky
summary: Dmytro Ivanovych Yavornytsky was a prominent Ukrainian academician, historian, archeologist, ethnographer, folklorist, and lexicographer, recognized for his extensive research on the Zaporozhian Cossacks and their history. He is often referred to as 'the father of the Zaporozhians' in historiography.

title: Dnieper
summary: The Dnieper, also known as the Dnipro, is a significant transboundary river in Europe, originating in Russia and flowing through Belarus and Ukraine to the Black Sea. It is the longest river in Ukraine and plays a crucial role in the country's economy and cultural identity.

title: Dnieper Ukraine
summary: Dnieper Ukraine, or Наддніпрянщина, refers to the territories flanking the middle course of the Dnieper River, integral to [[history-of-ukraine|Ukrainian history]] and identity. This region is often considered the heart of Ukraine and is historically significant due to its connection with the nation's past.

title: Dniester
summary: The Dniester is a transboundary river in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]], primarily flowing through Ukraine before continuing into Moldova and discharging into the Black Sea on Ukrainian territory. It serves as a significant geographical and historical landmark in the region.

title: Dniester Canyon
summary: The Dniester Canyon is a significant geological formation created by the Dniester River, located in southwestern Ukraine across several oblasts. It was designated as a national nature park in 2010, highlighting its ecological and geological importance.

title: Dnipro
summary: Dnipro is the fourth-largest city [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], located in the eastern part of the country along the Dnipro River. With a population of approximately one million, it serves as the administrative center of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast and has a rich historical and industrial significance.

title: Dnipro Art Museum
summary: The Dnipro Art Museum, located in [[dnieper|Dnipro]], [[ukraine|Ukraine]], is one of the oldest fine arts museums in the country, housing a diverse collection of approximately 8,500 artworks ranging from the 16th to the 21st centuries.

title: Dnipropetrovsk Oblast
summary: Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, also known as Dnipropetrovshchyna, is a province in southeastern Ukraine that serves as a crucial industrial region. Established on February 27, 1932, it has an estimated population of approximately 3,096,485 as of 2022, with a significant portion residing in major urban centers such as Dnipro and Kryvyi Rih.

title: Dnipropetrovsk Oblast State Administration
summary: The Dnipropetrovsk Oblast State Administration serves as the executive branch for Dnipropetrovsk Oblast [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], with the governor acting as its head. The position has evolved in response to the ongoing Russo-Ukrainian War, reflecting the region's strategic importance.

title: Dniprorudne
summary: Dniprorudne is a city located in the Vasylivka Raion of Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine, with a population of 17,736 as of 2022. It has been recognized as a city since 1970 and has played a significant role during the ongoing conflict [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

title: Donbas
summary: The Donbas is a historically significant industrial region located on the border between Russia and Ukraine, primarily within Ukraine itself. It has been a crucial coal mining area since the late 19th century and has been impacted by ongoing geopolitical conflicts, particularly the Russo-Ukrainian war.

title: Donets
summary: The Seversky Donets, also known as Siverskyi Donets, is a significant river located in eastern Ukraine, playing a crucial role in the region's ecology and economy. It is the fourth-longest river [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] and the largest in eastern Ukraine, flowing through key industrial areas and contributing to the water supply of major cities.

title: Donetsk
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Donetsk is an industrial city in eastern Ukraine, situated on the Kalmius River within Donetsk Oblast. Historically significant as the unofficial capital of the [[donbas|Donets Basin]], it has been a focal point of conflict during the Russo-Ukrainian War since 2014.

title: Donetsk International Airport
summary: Donetsk Sergei Prokofiev International Airport (IATA: DOK, ICAO: UKCC) was a significant airport located 10 km northwest of Donetsk, Ukraine, which was destroyed during the conflict in the Donbas region in 2014. Named after the composer Sergei Prokofiev, a native of the area, the airport has been repurposed for military use as of December 2025.

title: Donetsk Oblast
summary: Donetsk Oblast, known as Donechchyna, is an administrative region in eastern Ukraine, primarily located in the [[donbas|Donbas]] area. It has a significant historical and economic role within Ukraine, particularly as a coal-mining hub, although much of its territory is currently under Russian occupation.

title: Donetsk People's Republic
summary: The Donetsk People's Republic (DPR) is a self-proclaimed republic in eastern Ukraine, established in 2014 amid conflict and backed by Russia. It is considered a disputed territory and has been subject to international condemnation and lack of recognition.

title: Drohobych
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Drohobych is a city of regional significance located in Lviv Oblast, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of Drohobych Raion and hosting the Drohobych urban hromada. Historically significant as a trading post and industrial hub, it has a rich cultural heritage and notable historical figures associated with it.

title: DTEK
summary: DTEK is the largest private investor in Ukraine's energy sector, involved in electricity generation, coal and gas extraction, and energy trading. The company plays a crucial role in the development of renewable energy and supports Ukraine's energy infrastructure.

title: Dumka
summary: Dumka is a city located in the state of Jharkhand, India, serving as the headquarters of the Dumka district and the Santhal Pargana region. Established as a significant administrative center, Dumka has a rich history and cultural heritage, with connections to various ethnic groups and religions.

title: easter egg
summary: Easter eggs, also known as Paschal eggs, are decorated eggs associated with the Christian celebration of Easter, symbolizing the resurrection of Jesus. This tradition is particularly significant in Ukraine and other Central and Eastern European cultures, where the practice of dyeing and painting eggs has deep historical roots.

title: Eastern Europe
summary: Eastern Europe is a subregion of the European continent characterized by diverse geopolitical, cultural, and socio-economic aspects. It includes countries such as Ukraine, Belarus, and Russia, and has been shaped by historical influences including Eastern Christianity and the legacy of the Cold War.

title: Eastern Galicia
summary: Eastern Galicia is a historical region in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]] that forms part of modern-day Western Ukraine and Southeastern Poland. It is significant for its mixed population and its historical ties to both Ukrainian and Polish national identities.

title: economy of Ukraine
summary: The economy of Ukraine is characterized as a developing social market economy, featuring rich agricultural land, a diverse industrial base, and significant mineral resources. Despite these advantages, Ukraine faces challenges such as high corruption levels and slow economic reforms, contributing to its status as one of the poorest countries in Europe.

title: education in Ukraine
summary: Education in Ukraine is structured into multiple levels, beginning with preschool and culminating in postgraduate education. The system has undergone significant changes, including a transition to a 12-year schooling framework that started in September 2018.

title: elections in Ukraine
summary: Elections in Ukraine are conducted for the selection of the president, members of the Verkhovna Rada, and local government officials. The electoral process is characterized by a multi-party system and specific legal frameworks that govern the conduct of elections.

title: electricity in Ukraine
summary: Electricity generation in Ukraine is primarily nuclear, with a significant focus on energy security and decentralization, particularly in the context of the ongoing Russo-Ukrainian War. The country's electricity infrastructure has faced challenges, including damage from conflict, but efforts are underway to enhance resilience and integrate with European energy markets.

title: Energoatom
summary: Energoatom is the state-owned enterprise responsible for operating all nuclear power plants in Ukraine, making it the largest electricity producer in the country. Founded in October 1996, it plays a crucial role in meeting Ukraine's energy needs and ensuring nuclear safety.

title: energy in Ukraine
summary: Energy in Ukraine is characterized by a diverse mix primarily comprising gas, nuclear, oil, and coal. The country's energy policy emphasizes security, integration with the European Union, and the transition towards renewable sources amidst ongoing challenges, particularly due to the Russo-Ukrainian war.

title: Enerhodar
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Enerhodar is a city of regional significance located in the northwest of Zaporizhzhia Oblast, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], known primarily for its electricity generation industry, including coal-fired and nuclear power plants. As of 2022, it had an estimated population of 52,237 and has been under Russian occupation since early 2022.

title: Euromaidan
summary: Euromaidan, also known as the Maidan Uprising, was a significant wave of protests and civil unrest in Ukraine that began on 21 November 2013. Triggered by President [[viktor-yanukovych|Viktor Yanukovych]]'s decision to reject the European Union–Ukraine Association Agreement in favor of closer ties with Russia, the movement highlighted widespread discontent with government corruption and human rights violations, ultimately leading to the 2014 Revolution of Dignity.

title: European Solidarity
summary: European Solidarity is a [[political-party-in-ukraine|political party in Ukraine]], rooted in the parliamentary group Solidarity established in 2000 by Petro Poroshenko. The party has undergone several transformations and name changes, reflecting its evolving political stance and leadership, particularly in relation to Ukraine's European integration and governance reforms.

title: Eurovision Song Contest 2016
summary: The Eurovision Song Contest 2016 marked the 61st iteration of the annual music competition, featuring Ukraine's significant victory with the song '1944' performed by Jamala. The event took place in Stockholm, Sweden, and highlighted Ukraine's cultural contributions and the relevance of its music on an international stage.

title: Eurovision Song Contest 2017
summary: The Eurovision Song Contest 2017 marked the 62nd edition of the annual music competition, held in Kyiv, Ukraine. This event was notable for Ukraine's hosting role following its victory in the previous year and for the significant political context surrounding the participation of certain countries.

title: Evgeny Sokolov
summary: Evgeny Sokolov, born on 11 June 1984, is a professional road bicycle racer from Russia, known for his participation in competitive cycling events, including his tenure with the UCI ProTour team Bbox Bouygues Telecom.

title: Executed Renaissance
summary: The Executed Renaissance refers to a generation of Ukrainian artists and intellectuals active during the 1920s and early 1930s in the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic, whose cultural contributions were largely suppressed during [[donetsk|Stalin]]'s Great Terror. This period was marked by significant advancements in various artistic fields, ultimately leading to the tragic loss of many of its key figures.

title: Fastiv

summary: Fastiv is a city of regional significance located in the Kyiv Oblast of central Ukraine, known for its historical importance and as a significant transport hub. With a population of approximately 44,014 as of 2022, it plays a vital role in the economic and logistical landscape of Ukraine.

title: FC Dynamo Kyiv
summary: FC Dynamo Kyiv is a professional football club based in Kyiv, Ukraine, founded in 1927. The club has a rich history in both Soviet and Ukrainian football, consistently competing at the highest levels and achieving significant domestic and international success.

title: FC Zorya Luhansk
summary: FC Zorya Luhansk is a professional football club based in Luhansk, Ukraine, known for its historical significance and achievements in Ukrainian football. Due to the ongoing [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|Russo-Ukrainian War]], the club has been playing its home games in Zaporizhzhia since 2014.

title: Ferrexpo
summary: Ferrexpo plc is a Swiss-based commodity trading and mining company recognized as the third largest exporter of iron ore pellets globally, with significant operations in Ukraine. The company plays a crucial role in the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] mining sector, operating multiple iron ore mines and a pellet production facility in the central region of the country.

title: Fine Arts Museum Kharkiv
summary: The Kharkiv Art Museum, located in [[kharkiv-oblast|Kharkiv]], Ukraine, is one of the largest state collections of fine and applied arts in the country. Established in 1905, the museum has a rich history and a diverse collection that reflects the artistic heritage of Ukraine and beyond.

title: First Battle of Kharkov
summary: The First Battle of Kharkov, fought from 20 to 24 October 1941, was a significant conflict for control of Kharkov in the [[ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic|Ukrainian SSR]] during Operation Barbarossa. The battle involved the German 6th Army and the Soviet Southwestern Front, ultimately leading to the capture of the city by German forces.

title: First Partition of Poland
summary: The First Partition of Poland occurred in 1772 and marked the beginning of the end for the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which was ultimately dissolved by 1795. This event significantly impacted [[ukraine|Ukraine]], as it involved territorial changes that affected the region's political landscape.

title: flag of Ukraine
summary: The national flag of Ukraine, characterized by its blue and yellow horizontal bands, serves as a significant symbol of Ukrainian identity and sovereignty. Its history reflects the country's struggles for independence and national recognition.

title: foreign relations of Ukraine
summary: The foreign relations of Ukraine encompass its diplomatic engagements with various nations, emphasizing Euro-Atlantic integration and security partnerships, particularly in response to regional threats. Ukraine's foreign policy has evolved significantly, especially following the annexation of Crimea and the ongoing conflict with Russia.

title: full-scale Russo-Ukrainian war
summary: The full-scale Russo-Ukrainian war began on 24 February 2022 with Russia's invasion of Ukraine, marking the most significant military conflict in Europe since World War II. This war escalated from earlier hostilities that started in 2014 when Russia annexed Crimea and supported separatist movements in eastern Ukraine.

title: Gaidai
summary: The term 'Gaidai' encompasses several references, including a surname and educational institutions, as well as an asteroid. Its relevance extends to various fields, including academia and astronomy.

title: Galicia
summary: Galicia, a historical region that encompasses parts of modern southeastern Poland and western Ukraine, has significant ties to [[history-of-ukraine|Ukrainian history]] and culture. It was a prominent area during the medieval period, particularly as part of the Kingdom of Galicia–Volhynia, and later became a contested territory during various political upheavals in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]].

title: Geography of Ukraine
summary: Ukraine, the second-largest country in Europe, features a diverse geography that includes fertile plains, highlands, and a variety of climatic conditions. Its geographic location and natural resources significantly influence its agricultural productivity and environmental challenges.

title: Golden Gate
summary: The Golden Gate of Kyiv served as a principal entrance in the 11th-century fortifications of Kyiv, the capital of [[kievan-rus|Kievan Rus]]'. Originally constructed between 1017 and 1024, it has undergone several reconstructions and remains a significant historical and cultural symbol [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

title: Gorodok
summary: Gorodok is a term that can refer to various locations and entities, particularly in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]], including connections to Ukraine. It encompasses several inhabited localities, historical military operations, and cultural references.

title: Great Famine
summary: The Great Famine, specifically the Holodomor, refers to the devastating famine that occurred in Ukraine from 1932 to 1933, resulting in millions of deaths and significant historical implications for the region.

title: Green Ukraine
summary: Green Ukraine, also referred to as Zelenyi Klyn or Zakytaishchyna, is a historical region in the Russian Far East, situated between the Amur River and the Pacific Ocean, with significant Ukrainian settlement during the Russian Empire's expansion. This area, characterized by its geographical features and rich cultural history, played a notable role in the [[ukrainian-diaspora|Ukrainian diaspora]] and national movements in the early 20th century.

title: Grigory Leps
summary: Grigory Leps, born Grigory Viktorovich Lepsveridze on 16 July 1962, is a prominent Russian singer-songwriter of Georgian descent, recognized for his deep baritone voice and evolution from Russian chanson to soft rock. His career has been marked by significant financial success and controversial political engagements, particularly in relation to Ukraine.

title: Gritsenko

title: gromada

title: Gulag
summary: The Gulag was a system of labor camps in [[soviet-union|the Soviet Union]], primarily operational from the 1930s to the early 1950s, which played a significant role in political repression. This system affected millions, including many Ukrainians, who were subjected to forced labor and harsh conditions.

title: Gulliver's Travels
summary: Gulliver's Travels is a 1726 satirical prose novel by Jonathan Swift that critiques human nature through the adventures of Lemuel Gulliver in various fantastical lands. Its themes and insights remain relevant in literary discussions, including those in Ukraine, where its social commentary resonates with ongoing societal reflections.

title: Haidamaka
summary: The Haidamaka, also known as haidamakas or haidamaky, were Ukrainian Cossack paramilitaries active in the eastern regions of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth during the 18th century. Their emergence was fueled by ethnic, social, and religious tensions, leading to several significant uprisings against Polish nobility.

title: Halič
summary: Halič is a village and municipality located in the Lučenec District of the Banská Bystrica Region in Slovakia. Its historical significance and demographic composition, including a [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] minority, highlight its relevance to the cultural landscape of the region.

title: Halych
summary: Halych is a historic city located on the Dniester River in western Ukraine, known for its role as the capital of the Principality of Halych and the Kingdom of Galicia–Volhynia until the early 14th century. Today, it is a small town in the Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast, retaining its historical significance and name.

title: Hanna Malyar
summary: Hanna Vasylivna Maliar is a Ukrainian lawyer and educator who served as a Deputy Minister of Defense from August 4, 2021, until September 18, 2023, under Prime Minister [[denys-shmyhal|Denys Shmyhal]]. Her work has been significant in the context of Ukraine's ongoing defense challenges, particularly during the full-scale invasion by Russia in 2022.

title: Henichesk
summary: Henichesk is a port city situated along the Sea of Azov in [[kherson-oblast|Kherson Oblast]], southern Ukraine, functioning as the administrative center of Henichesk Raion. As of January 2022, it had an estimated population of 18,889 and has been under Russian occupation since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

title: Hennadiy Avdyeyenko
summary: Hennadiy Valentynovych Avdyeyenko is a retired high jumper from Ukraine, born on November 4, 1963, in Odessa. He achieved significant success in athletics, representing both [[soviet-union|the USSR]] and Ukraine, and is known for winning gold medals at the Olympics and World Championships.

title: Heorhii Narbut
summary: Heorhiy Ivanovych Narbut was a prominent Ukrainian graphic artist known for his significant contributions to the visual identity of the [[ukrainian-peoples-republic|Ukrainian People's Republic]] through his designs of banknotes, postage stamps, and the national coat of arms.

title: hetman
summary: Hetman is a historical political and military title from Central and [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]], particularly significant [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] as the title of the head of the Cossack state following the [[khmelnytsky-uprising|Khmelnytsky Uprising]] of 1648. The title has roots in various cultures and has evolved over time, reflecting the military and political landscape of the region.

title: Hetmanate

title: history of Crimea
summary: The history of Crimea is marked by its strategic location and diverse cultural influences, particularly its connections to Ukraine. From ancient Greek colonies to the establishment of the Crimean Khanate and later incorporation into the Russian Empire, Crimea has played a significant role in regional dynamics and [[history-of-ukraine|Ukrainian history]].

title: history of Kyiv
summary: The history of Kyiv, the capital of Ukraine, spans over a millennium and is marked by its significance as a political, cultural, and economic center throughout various historical periods. The city's origins are debated, with archaeological evidence suggesting settlements dating back to 25,000 BC and its official founding recognized in 482 AD.

title: history of the Cossacks
summary: The history of the Cossacks is marked by the emergence of semi-autonomous, militarized communities in the steppe regions north of the Black and Caspian seas, particularly influencing Ukraine's political and military landscape from the late medieval period onward.

title: history of the Jews in Ukraine
summary: The history of the Jews in Ukraine spans over a millennium, marked by periods of both flourishing communities and severe persecution. Jewish presence in Ukraine is significant, contributing to the cultural and social landscape of the region, particularly during the times of [[kievan-rus|Kievan Rus]]' and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.
aliases: history of the Jews of Ukraine

title: history of Ukraine
type: history of a country or state
summary: The history of Ukraine encompasses a rich tapestry of cultural, political, and social developments from prehistoric times to the present, highlighting its significance in Eastern Europe and its interactions with various civilizations and empires. Key events include the establishment of Kievan Rus', the impact of foreign dominations, the emergence of [[ukrainian-nationalism|Ukrainian nationalism]], and the struggle for independence in the 20th century.

title: history of Ukrainian nationality
summary: The history of Ukrainian nationality is deeply rooted in the medieval kingdom of Kievan Rus', which existed from the 9th to the 12th centuries and laid the foundation for the Eastern Slavic nations, including Ukraine. This entry explores the development of Ukrainian identity through various historical phases, including prehistory, the rise of the Slavs, the establishment of Kievan Rus', and the subsequent emergence of the Kingdom of Ruthenia.

title: Holodomor
summary: The Holodomor, or Ukrainian famine, was a catastrophic man-made famine that occurred in Soviet Ukraine from 1932 to 1933, resulting in the deaths of millions of Ukrainians. This event is a significant part of Ukraine's history and has been recognized by various nations as a genocide against the Ukrainian people.

title: hopak
summary: Hopak is a traditional Ukrainian folk dance that originated as a male dance among the [[zaporozhian-cossacks|Zaporozhian Cossacks]] and has evolved to include couples and mixed groups. It is often celebrated as the 'National Dance of [[ukraine|Ukraine]]' and is performed by various dance ensembles both [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] and internationally.

title: Horishni Plavni

title: Hoverla
summary: Mount Hoverla, standing at 2,061 metres (6,762 ft), is the highest mountain [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] and is situated within the [[ukrainian-carpathians|Ukrainian Carpathians]]. It is a significant natural landmark in the Chornohora region, attracting tourists and extreme sports enthusiasts alike.

title: Hrushevsky Street
summary: Hrushevsky Street is a street name predominantly found [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], honoring the prominent Ukrainian historian and political figure Mykhailo Hrushevsky.

title: Hryhorii Skovoroda
summary: Hryhorii Skovoroda was an influential Ukrainian philosopher, poet, and composer born on December 3, 1722, in the village of Chornukhy, now in [[poltava-oblast|Poltava Oblast]], Ukraine. His works and teachings, which blended various languages and philosophical traditions, have left a lasting impact on Ukrainian literature and culture.

title: Hryshko National Botanical Garden
summary: The M. M. Hryshko National Botanical Garden is a significant botanical garden located in Kyiv, Ukraine, under the auspices of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine. Established in 1936, it features a diverse collection of plant species and serves as a popular recreational area for residents and visitors.
aliases: M. M. Hryshko National Botanical Garden

title: hryvnia
summary: The hryvnia is the official currency of Ukraine, introduced on 2 September 1996. It is subdivided into 100 kopiyka and is named after a historical measure of weight from Kievan Rus'.

title: human rights in Ukraine
type: human rights by country or territory
summary: Human rights in Ukraine encompass the fundamental rights of individuals within the country, reflecting a complex historical and contemporary landscape influenced by political, social, and military factors. Recent developments, particularly due to the ongoing conflict with Russia, have significantly impacted the state of human rights in Ukraine.

title: Hungary–Ukraine relations
summary: Hungary–Ukraine relations have evolved since the early 1990s, shaped by historical ties and contemporary political issues, particularly concerning the rights of the Hungarian minority [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s Zakarpattia region. The bilateral relationship has experienced significant fluctuations due to language laws, military base controversies, and energy agreements.

title: Hutsuls
summary: The Hutsuls are an East Slavic ethnic group primarily located in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]] and northern Romania, recognized as a subgroup of [[ukrainians|Ukrainians]] and considered part of the broader Ukrainian ethnicity. They inhabit the region known as Hutsulshchyna, which is characterized by its unique culture, language, and history.

title: Igor Girkin
summary: Igor Vsevolodovich Girkin, also known as Igor Ivanovich Strelkov, is a Russian military veteran and former Federal Security Service officer who played a significant role in the Russian annexation of Crimea and the subsequent conflict in eastern [[ukraine|Ukraine]], particularly in the [[donbas|Donbas]] region. His actions have led to multiple international sanctions and a life sentence in absentia for his involvement in the downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17.

title: Igor Sikorsky
summary: Igor Ivanovich Sikorsky (25 May 1889 – 26 October 1972) was a notable aviation pioneer of Ukrainian origin, recognized for his contributions to both helicopter and fixed-wing aircraft design. His early life in Kyiv, Russian Empire, significantly influenced his later achievements in aviation.

title: Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute
summary: The Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute, also known as KPI, is a prominent national public technological university located in Kyiv, Ukraine. Established in 1898, it has significantly contributed to the scientific and technological advancement of the country.

summary: Ihor Kolomoyskyi is a prominent Ukrainian-born Israeli billionaire businessman and former oligarch, known for his significant influence in Ukraine's economic and political landscape. He co-founded PrivatBank and has been involved in various sectors, including media and finance, while facing numerous allegations of corruption.

summary: Illich Steel & Iron Works, located in Mariupol, is the second largest metallurgical enterprise in Ukraine, known for its diverse steel production and significant historical contributions to the industry.

title: Independence Day of Ukraine
summary: Independence Day of Ukraine, celebrated on 24 August, is a significant state holiday commemorating the Declaration of Independence in 1991. This day reflects Ukraine's historical journey towards sovereignty and has evolved in public perception and celebration over the years.

title: Independent Ukraine
summary: Independent Ukraine is a political pamphlet authored by Mykola Mikhnovsky in 1900, advocating for a sovereign Ukrainian state. This work is significant in the context of [[ukraine|Ukraine]]'s national identity and political aspirations.

title: Industry in Ukraine

summary: Industry in Ukraine is characterized by a robust material and technical foundation, with significant contributions to the country's economy. As of 2007, the sector employed over 3.6 million individuals and generated substantial profits, reflecting its importance in the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] economic landscape.

title: Intercession of the Theotokos
summary: The Intercession of the Theotokos is a Christian feast dedicated to the Mother of God, observed on October 14 in the Eastern Orthodox and Byzantine Catholic Churches. Particularly significant in Ukraine, the feast highlights the protective role of the Theotokos and is closely associated with Ukrainian cultural and historical identity.

title: Intermarium
summary: Intermarium was a geopolitical initiative proposed by Józef Piłsudski after World War I aimed at uniting the lands of the former Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth into a federation. This plan included various Central and Eastern European nations, including Ukraine, and sought to counterbalance Russian and German imperialism.

title: Interpipe Group
summary: Interpipe Group is a Ukrainian industrial company recognized as a global manufacturer of steel pipes and railway wheels, with its headquarters and production facilities situated in Nikopol, Ukraine. The company plays a significant role in the carbon steel pipes and railway products markets, employing approximately 11,000 individuals.

title: Irpin
summary: Irpin is a city located on the Irpin River in Bucha Raion, Kyiv Oblast, northern Ukraine, known for its proximity to the capital Kyiv and its significant historical and cultural heritage. The city has a population of approximately 65,167 as of 2022 and has been notably impacted by the [[2022-russian-invasion-of-ukraine|2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]].

title: Iryna Venediktova
summary: Iryna Venediktova is a prominent Ukrainian politician, lawyer, and academic known for her significant roles in Ukraine's legal and political landscape, including serving as the first female Prosecutor General. As of November 2022, she holds the position of Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of [[ukraine|Ukraine]] to Switzerland and Liechtenstein.

title: Iryna Vilde
summary: Iryna Vilde, born Daryna Polotniuk, was a prominent Ukrainian and Soviet writer known for her significant contributions to Ukrainian literature. Her works, which explore the complexities of life in Western Ukraine, are now regarded as classics.

title: Ivan Aivazovsky
summary: Ivan Konstantinovich Aivazovsky was a prominent Russian Romantic painter, renowned for his mastery in marine art. Born in Feodosia, Crimea, to Armenian parents, Aivazovsky's works are significant within the Ukrainian context, with many of his paintings housed in Ukrainian museums.

title: Ivan Franko
summary: Ivan Yakovych Franko was a prominent Ukrainian poet, writer, and political activist, recognized as a key figure in the development of modern Ukrainian literature and socialist thought. His contributions include pioneering detective novels and modern poetry, as well as translating significant works into Ukrainian.

title: Ivan Franko Museum
summary: The Ivan Franko Museum is a dedicated institution honoring the legacy of Ukrainian writer and poet Ivan Franko, located in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada. It serves as a cultural hub for the Ukrainian community and operates primarily through volunteer efforts.

title: Ivan Franko National Academic Drama Theater
summary: The Ivan Franko National Academic Drama Theater, located in Kyiv, is a significant institution in [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] culture, founded in 1920. It has been a platform for renowned artists and has produced a diverse repertoire of national and world classics.

title: Ivan Karabyts
summary: Ivan Fedorovych Karabyts was a prominent [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] composer and conductor, recognized as a People's Artist of Ukraine. His contributions to music, particularly in the context of Ukrainian cultural development, have left a lasting impact.

title: Ivan Kotliarevskyi
summary: Ivan Petrovych Kotliarevsky was a prominent Ukrainian writer, poet, playwright, and social activist, recognized as the pioneer of modern Ukrainian literature. His notable work, the poem Eneida, is a travesty of Virgil's Aeneid and marks a significant milestone in the use of vernacular Ukrainian as a literary language.

title: Ivan Malkovych
summary: Ivan Antonovych Malkovych is a prominent Ukrainian poet and publisher, recognized for his contributions to [[ukrainian-literature|Ukrainian literature]] and his role in promoting high-quality literary works through his publishing house, 'A-BA-BA-HA-LA-MA-HA.' He was awarded the [[shevchenko-national-prize|Shevchenko National Prize]] in 2017.

title: Ivan Mazepa
summary: Ivan Stepanovych Mazepa (30 March [O.S. 20 March] 1639 – 2 October [O.S. 21 September] 1709) was a prominent Ukrainian military and political leader who served as hetman of the [[cossack-hetmanate|Cossack Hetmanate]] from 1687 to 1709, known for his efforts in restoring Ukraine's political and economic stability following the Ruin.

title: Ivan Sirko
summary: Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko (c. 1605 – August 11, 1680) was a prominent Zaporozhian Cossack military leader and Koshovyi Otaman, renowned for his military campaigns against the Ottoman Empire and the Crimean Khanate. His legacy is closely tied to Ukraine's history, particularly through his undefeated record in battle and his role in significant military engagements during the 17th century.

title: Ivano-Frankivsk

summary: Ivano-Frankivsk is a city of regional significance in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast and Ivano-Frankivsk Raion. With a population of approximately 238,196 in 2022, it has a rich historical background and diverse cultural influences.

title: Ivano-Frankivsk National Medical University
summary: Ivano-Frankivsk National Medical University is a state-sponsored higher education institution located in Ivano-Frankivsk, Ukraine, established in 1945. It is recognized for its medical education programs and holds a significant position in the Ukrainian educational landscape as a designated 'National Medical University.'

title: Ivano-Frankivsk National Technical University of Oil and Gas
summary: The Ivano-Frankivsk National Technical University of Oil and Gas is a higher education institution located in [[ivano-frankivsk|Ivano-Frankivsk]], [[ukraine|Ukraine]], established in 1967. It specializes in training professionals for the oil and gas sectors while also offering programs in economics, management, and law relevant to the energy industry.

title: Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast
summary: Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast is a region in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], with its administrative center in the city of Ivano-Frankivsk. As of 2022, it has a population of 1,351,822 and is known for its mountainous terrain and rich cultural heritage.

title: Ivano-Frankivsk Raion
summary: Ivano-Frankivsk Raion is a district located in Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast, Ukraine, established in July 2020 as part of administrative reform. The district's center is the city of Ivano-Frankivsk and it has a population of approximately 556,104 as of 2022.

title: Iziaslav
summary: Iziaslav refers to multiple subjects related to Ukraine, including a city and a former administrative region, as well as notable historical figures. The name is significant within the context of Ukrainian history and geography.

title: Izmail
summary: Izmail is a city and municipality located on the Danube River in Odesa Oblast, Ukraine. It serves as the administrative center of Izmail Raion and is recognized as the largest port in the Danube Delta, playing a significant role [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s economy and maritime activities.

title: Jamala
summary: Susana Alimivna Jamaladinova, known as Jamala, is a prominent Ukrainian singer who gained international recognition by winning the Eurovision Song Contest in 2016 with her song '1944'. Her work is deeply connected to her Crimean Tatar heritage and the historical context of Crimea, particularly the deportation of the Crimean Tatars.

title: judicial system of Ukraine
summary: The judicial system of Ukraine, established under the 1996 Constitution, has undergone significant reforms since the country's independence in 1991. Despite improvements, issues such as corruption and political influence continue to affect its functionality.

title: Kamianets-Podilskyi

summary: Kamianets-Podilskyi is a city of regional significance in western Ukraine, located on the Smotrych River. title: Karpaty
summary: Karpaty refers to various subjects, primarily associated with the Carpathian Mountains and several locations in Ukraine, as well as sports teams and other geographic references.

title: Kerch Strait incident
summary: The Kerch Strait incident, occurring on 25 November 2018, involved the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB) coast guard firing upon and capturing three Ukrainian Navy vessels as they attempted to transit from the Black Sea to the Sea of Azov. This event marked the first direct engagement between Russian and Ukrainian forces during the ongoing [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|Russo-Ukrainian War]] and highlighted the tensions surrounding maritime access to Ukrainian ports.

title: Kharkiv
summary: Kharkiv, the second-largest city [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], serves as the administrative center of Kharkiv Oblast and Kharkiv Raion. It has a rich history as a cultural, industrial, and educational hub, significantly influencing the development of Ukrainian identity and politics.

title: Kharkiv National University of Radioelectronics
summary: Kharkiv National University of Radioelectronics (NURE) is a prominent state-sponsored technological university located in Kharkiv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. Established in 1930, it is recognized as one of the oldest institutions of its kind in the country, serving approximately 7,000 students.

title: Kharkiv Oblast
summary: Kharkiv Oblast, also known as Kharkivshchyna, is a province located in eastern Ukraine. It is the third-most populous oblast in the country and plays a significant role [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s industrial and agricultural sectors.

title: Kharkiv Tractor Plant
summary: The Kharkiv Tractor Plant (KhTZ or HTZ) is a significant agricultural machinery manufacturer located in Kharkiv, Ukraine. title: Kherson

title: Kherson Art Museum
summary: The Kherson Art Museum, officially known as the Oleksii Shovkunenko Kherson Regional Art Museum, is an art institution located in Kherson, Ukraine, established on May 27, 1978. summary: Kherson Oblast is a province in southern Ukraine, situated just north of Crimea, with Kherson as its administrative center.
