title: Khmelnytsky Uprising
summary: The Khmelnytsky Uprising was a significant Cossack rebellion that occurred between 1648 and 1657 in the eastern territories of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, primarily in [[dnieper-ukraine|Dnieper Ukraine]]. Led by Cossack Hetman Bohdan Khmelnytsky, the uprising resulted in a Cossack victory and the establishment of the Cossack Hetmanate, marking a pivotal moment [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s history and its relations with Poland and Russia.

title: Khmelnytskyi
summary: Khmelnytskyi is a city in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of Khmelnytskyi Oblast and Khmelnytskyi Raion. With a population of 274,452 as of 2022, it is the second-largest city in the historical region of Podolia, following [[vinnytsia|Vinnytsia]].

title: Khmelnytskyi Oblast
summary: Khmelnytskyi Oblast is a province located in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], encompassing parts of the historical regions of western Podolia and southern Volhynia. The oblast, with an estimated population of around 1,228,829 as of 2022, serves as an important administrative and cultural region within Ukraine.

title: Khortytsia
summary: Khortytsia is the largest island on the Dnieper River, measuring 12.5 km in length and up to 2.5 km in width. Located within the city limits of Zaporizhzhia, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], it is a significant historical site, particularly for its connection to the [[zaporozhian-cossacks|Zaporozhian Cossacks]] and its unique biodiversity.

title: Khotyn
summary: Khotyn is a city located in Dnistrovskyi Raion, [[chernivtsi-oblast|Chernivtsi Oblast]], in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], known for its historical significance and architectural landmarks, including the Khotyn Fortress. It has a population of approximately 8,936 as of 2022 and serves as the administrative center of the Khotyn urban hromada.

title: Khotyn Fortress
summary: Khotyn Fortress is a significant fortification complex situated on the right bank of the Dniester River in Khotyn, Chernivtsi Oblast, Ukraine. Its historical relevance is underscored by its strategic location and extensive history, which includes periods of control by various powers, including Kievan Rus', Moldavia, the Ottoman Empire, and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

title: Khotyn National Nature Park
summary: Khotyn National Nature Park is a significant national park [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], encompassing a portion of the Dniester River Canyon and the Dniester River Reservoir, located in Chernivtsi Oblast near the Romanian border.

title: Khotyn Raion
summary: Khotyn Raion was an administrative district located in the southern part of Chernivtsi Oblast, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], bordering Romania. It was part of the historical [[bessarabia|Bessarabia]] region and was dissolved on July 18, 2020, during an administrative reform that restructured the raions of Chernivtsi Oblast.

title: Khrushchyovka
summary: Khrushchyovkas are a series of low-cost, multi-story apartment buildings that emerged in the Soviet Union during the leadership of Nikita Khrushchev in the early 1960s. These structures played a significant role in addressing the housing crisis in Ukraine and other Soviet republics, symbolizing the architectural shift towards industrialized construction methods.

title: Kievan Rus'
summary: Kievan Rus', also referred to as Kyivan Rus', was the inaugural East Slavic state and a collective of principalities in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]] from the late 9th to the mid-13th century. It played a crucial role in shaping the cultural and political landscape of Ukraine and the surrounding region.

title: Kingdom of Galicia–Volhynia
summary: The Kingdom of Galicia–Volhynia, also referred to as the Kingdom of Ruthenia or Kingdom of Rus', was a significant medieval state in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]] that existed from 1199 to 1349, primarily within the territory of modern-day [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. It emerged from the fragmentation of [[kievan-rus|Kievan Rus]]' and played a crucial role in the region's political landscape during its existence.

title: Kirovohrad Oblast
summary: Kirovohrad Oblast, also known as Kirovohradshchyna, is a province located in central Ukraine, with Kropyvnytskyi serving as its administrative center. The oblast has a population of 903,712 as of 2022 and is recognized as Ukraine's second least populated oblast.

title: kobzar
summary: A kobzar was an itinerant bard in Ukraine, known for singing accompanied by the kobza, a traditional stringed instrument. This occupation emerged during the Cossack Era in the 16th century and became predominantly associated with blind musicians by the 1800s.

title: Kolomyjka
summary: Kolomyika is a [[music-of-ukraine|Ukrainian music]] genre characterized by a lively folk dance and humorous rhymed verses. Originating from the town of Kolomyia in western Ukraine, it has historical significance among Ukrainians and Poles and continues to be a vibrant part of cultural festivities in Ukraine.

title: Kramatorsk
summary: Kramatorsk is a city in eastern Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Kramatorsk Raion in Donetsk Oblast. It plays a significant role as an industrial hub and has been a focal point during the Russo-Ukrainian war.

title: Kramatorsk railway station attack
summary: The Kramatorsk railway station attack occurred on 8 April 2022, when a Russian missile strike targeted civilians in Kramatorsk, Ukraine, resulting in 63 fatalities, including 9 children, and 150 injuries. This incident highlights the ongoing violence during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, which began on 24 February 2022.

title: Kremenchuk
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Kremenchuk is an industrial city located in central [[ukraine|Ukraine]] along the Dnipro River, serving as the administrative center of Kremenchuk Raion and Kremenchuk urban hromada in Poltava Oblast. With an estimated population of approximately 215,271 in 2022, it is recognized as a significant industrial hub in Ukraine and Eastern Europe.

title: Kremenchuk Reservoir
summary: The Kremenchuk Reservoir is a significant water body located on the Dnieper River within the Ukrainian oblasts of Poltava, Cherkasy, and Kirovohrad. It serves multiple purposes, including irrigation, flood control, fishing, and transportation.

title: Kremenets Castle
summary: Kremenets Castle, located in the city of Kremenets, [[ternopil-oblast|Ternopil Oblast]], [[ukraine|Ukraine]], is a historic fortress known for its strategic significance and architectural features. Built primarily of limestone, it has served as a stronghold against various invasions throughout its history.

title: Kreminna
summary: Kreminna is a city located in [[siverskodonetsk|Sievierodonetsk]] Raion, [[luhansk-oblast|Luhansk Oblast]], in eastern Ukraine. Established in 1680, it has been significantly impacted by the ongoing Russo-Ukrainian War, particularly since the Russian invasion in February 2022.

title: Kremlin
summary: The Moscow Kremlin, a fortified complex in Moscow, Russia, serves as a significant historical and political symbol. It is not only a UNESCO World Heritage site but also represents the seat of power for the Russian government, influencing [[ukraine|Ukraine]]'s historical and political landscape, especially during periods of conflict and governance.

title: Kropyvnytskyi
summary: Kropyvnytskyi is a city located in central Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of [[kirovohrad-oblast|Kirovohrad Oblast]]. With a population of 219,676 as of 2022, it has a rich history marked by various name changes and significant cultural contributions to Ukraine.

title: Krymske
summary: Krymske refers to several locations within Ukraine, each with distinct administrative affiliations. These places are significant in their respective regions, contributing to the cultural and geographical diversity of Ukraine.

title: Kryvbas
summary: Kryvbas, or the Kryvyi Rih Iron Ore Basin, is a significant economic and historical region [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] known for its extensive iron ore mining and steel industry. Located primarily around the city of Kryvyi Rih, it is recognized as the leading iron ore region in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]].

title: Kryvorivnia
summary: Kryvorivnia is a village located in the Verkhovyna Raion of the Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], recognized as a cultural center for the Hutsul people. It serves as a significant site for both summer and winter traditions among this ethnic group.

title: Kryvyi Rih
summary: Kryvyi Rih is a significant city located in central Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Kryvyi Rih Raion in [[dnipropetrovsk-oblast|Dnipropetrovsk Oblast]]. With a population of approximately 603,904 as of 2022, it ranks as the seventh-most populous city in Ukraine and is notable for its extensive industrial history and geographical features.

title: Kryvyi Rih Metrotram
summary: The Kryvyi Rih Metrotram, officially known as the Kryvyi Rih Rapid Tram, is a rapid transit light rail system located in Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine's seventh-largest city. It serves as a significant component of the city's public transportation network, with a mix of underground and surface routes.

title: Kryvyi Rih National University
summary: Kryvyi Rih National University is a public higher education institution located in Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine, established in 1922. The university has undergone several transformations and currently comprises seven faculties and five institutes, reflecting its significant role in the educational landscape of Ukraine.

title: Kryzhopil
summary: Kryzhopil is a rural settlement located in Tulchyn Raion, Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine, with a population of 8,479 as of 2022. Previously, it served as the administrative center of the former Kryzhopil Raion until the administrative reform in 2020.

title: Kupala Night
summary: Kupala Night, also known as Ivan Kupala, is a significant folk holiday celebrated in Ukraine and other Slavic countries, coinciding with the summer solstice and the Christian feast of St. John the Baptist. The holiday features various rituals associated with water, fire, and herbs, reflecting its pre-Christian origins and cultural significance.

title: Kutia
summary: Kutia, also known as kutya, is a ceremonial grain dish in syrup that holds significant cultural importance in [[ukrainian-cuisine|Ukrainian cuisine]], particularly during the Christmas season. It is traditionally made with wheatberries, poppy seeds, and honey, reflecting ancient rituals and customs.

title: Kyiv
summary: Kyiv, the capital and largest city of Ukraine, is situated in the north-central region of the country along both banks of the Dnieper River. With a population of 2,952,301 as of January 2022, it serves as a significant industrial, scientific, educational, and cultural hub in Ukraine and Eastern Europe.

title: Kyiv City Ballet
summary: Kyiv City Ballet is an independent ballet company from [[ukraine|Ukraine]], currently based in Paris due to the ongoing conflict [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]. Founded in 2012, the troupe continues to perform and tour internationally, showcasing a diverse repertoire.

title: Kyiv City State Administration
summary: The Kyiv City State Administration, abbreviated as KMDA, is the national-level governmental body responsible for the administration of Kyiv, the capital of Ukraine. Following the onset of the Russian invasion in 2022, it was restructured into the Kyiv City Military Administration, reflecting its critical role during wartime governance.

title: Kyiv Fortress
summary: The Kyiv Fortress, also known as the New Pechersk Fortress, is a significant historical and architectural monument located in Kyiv, Ukraine. Constructed from the 17th to the 19th centuries, it represents a complex of fortifications that played a vital role in the city's defense and military history.

title: Kyiv Metro
summary: The Kyiv Metro is a rapid transit system located in Kyiv, Ukraine, operated by the city-owned company Kyivskyi Metropoliten. Opened on 6 November 1960, it was the first metro system in Ukraine and remains a vital component of the city's public transportation network.

title: Kyiv Music Fest
summary: The Kyiv Music Fest is an annual international music festival held in Kyiv, Ukraine, dedicated to showcasing modern Ukrainian classical music and promoting Ukrainian musicians within the global arts context. Established in 1990, the festival has become a significant cultural event [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

title: Kyiv National Academic Theatre of Operetta
summary: The Kyiv National Academic Theatre of Operetta is a prominent theatre located in Kyiv, Ukraine, established in 1934. It plays a significant role in the cultural landscape of Ukraine, particularly in the genre of operetta.

title: Kyiv National Economic University named after Vadym Hetman
summary: Kyiv National Economic University named after Vadym Hetman is a prominent self-governing public university located in Kyiv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], founded in 1906. It is recognized as a leading institution for economic [[education-in-ukraine|education in Ukraine]] and has been ranked highly in both national and international assessments.
aliases: Kyiv National Economics University named after Vadym Hetman

title: Kyiv National University of Culture and Arts
summary: The Kyiv National University of Culture and Arts (KNUCA) is a prominent educational institution located in Kyiv, Ukraine, recognized for its high level of accreditation and diverse academic programs in culture and arts.

title: Kyiv Oblast
summary: Kyiv Oblast, also known as Kyivshchyna, is a province in central and northern Ukraine that encircles the city of Kyiv. It plays a significant role in Ukraine's urban economy and transportation, with a population of approximately 1,795,079 as of 2022.

title: Kyiv offensive
summary: The term 'Kyiv offensive' refers to two significant military campaigns in [[history-of-ukraine|Ukrainian history]], specifically during the Polish–Soviet War in 1920 and as part of the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

title: Kyiv Pechersk Lavra
summary: The Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, also known as the Kyiv Monastery of the Caves, is a significant Eastern Orthodox monastery located in Kyiv, Ukraine. Founded in 1051, it has played a crucial role in the history of Eastern Christianity in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]].

title: Kyiv Post
summary: Kyiv Post is the first and most notable English-language newspaper in Ukraine, founded in 1995. It serves as a significant source of news and information about Ukraine, particularly for expatriates and international audiences.

title: Kyiv Zhuliany International Airport
summary: Kyiv Zhuliany International Airport, officially known as Igor Sikorsky Kyiv International Airport, is one of the two main passenger airports serving the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv. Located approximately seven kilometers southwest of the city center, it plays a significant role in both passenger and business aviation in Ukraine.

title: Kyiv Zoo
summary: Kyiv Zoo, the largest zoo in Kyiv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], and one of the largest in the [[post-soviet-states|former Soviet Union]], spans approximately 40 hectares and is home to around 2,600 animals from 328 species. The zoo plays a significant role in wildlife preservation and research [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], attracting about 280,000 visitors each year.
aliases: Kyiv Zoological Park of National Importance

title: Kyivstar
summary: Kyivstar is a prominent Ukrainian telecommunications operator providing a range of voice and data services, including 4G LTE, across Ukraine. As of 2024, it serves approximately 24 million mobile subscribers and has expanded its services to include partnerships with international entities such as Starlink.

title: Latin Church in Ukraine
summary: The Latin Church in Ukraine (LCiU), also known as the Roman Catholic Church in Ukraine (RCCiU), represents the Latin branch of the Catholic Church in Ukraine, one of four sui iuris Catholic churches in the country. Established since the 10th century, the Latin Church has played a significant role in Ukraine's religious, cultural, and historical development.

title: law of Ukraine
summary: The law of Ukraine encompasses primary legislation enacted by the Verkhovna Rada, the national parliament, and requires presidential approval for promulgation. These laws are integral to the legal framework of Ukraine, supporting the Constitution and including various codified laws.

title: Leonid Kravchuk
summary: Leonid Makarovych Kravchuk was a prominent Ukrainian politician who served as the first [[president-of-ukraine|president of Ukraine]] from December 5, 1991, to July 19, 1994, playing a crucial role in the country's independence from the Soviet Union. His presidency was marked by significant political and economic challenges, including the management of Ukraine's nuclear arsenal and a severe economic crisis.

title: Leonid Kuchma
summary: Leonid Danylovych Kuchma is a prominent Ukrainian politician who served as the second president of Ukraine from 19 July 1994 to 23 January 2005. His presidency is noted for economic stabilization and improved relations with Russia, but also for democratic backsliding and increased oligarchic influence.

title: Les Kurbas
summary: Oleksandr-Zenon Stepanovych Kurbas (25 February 1887 – 3 November 1937) was a significant Ukrainian theater and movie director, recognized as one of the most influential figures in 20th-century Ukrainian theater. He played a pivotal role in the Soviet theater avant-garde and is remembered for his contributions to [[ukrainian-avant-garde|Ukrainian avant-garde]] art and the [[executed-renaissance|Executed Renaissance]].

title: Lesya Ukrainka
summary: Lesya Ukrainka, born Larysa Petrivna Kosach on 25 February 1871, was a prominent Ukrainian writer known for her poetry and plays, as well as her activism for political, civil, and women's rights. Her works and life are deeply intertwined with the cultural and historical context of Ukraine.

title: LGBT rights in Ukraine
type: LGBT rights by country or territory
summary: LGBT rights in Ukraine have evolved significantly since the country's independence in 1991, with gradual increases in visibility and political organization within the LGBTQ community. Despite some legislative advancements, challenges remain, particularly regarding the recognition of same-sex relationships and protections against discrimination.

title: Liberal Party of Ukraine
summary: The Liberal Party of Ukraine (LPU) is a political party founded on September 12, 1991, in Donetsk, known for promoting liberal values and reforms [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]. It has a significant membership base and was the first liberal party in the post-Soviet space to be recognized by Liberal International.

title: Little Russia
summary: Little Russia, also referred to as Lesser Russia or Malorussia, is a historical term that has been used to describe Ukraine, particularly in the context of its relationship with Russia. The term has evolved over centuries and is now considered outdated and often offensive in contemporary Ukrainian discourse.

title: local government in Ukraine
summary: Local government in Ukraine is structured around two main systems that reflect the country's administrative divisions. This framework is governed by the Constitution and specific laws, enabling local councils and state administrations to manage community affairs and implement local governance.

title: Luhansk
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Luhansk is a city of regional significance located in eastern [[ukraine|Ukraine]], specifically within the Donbas region. As of 2022, it is the 12th-largest city [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], with a population of approximately 397,677.

title: Luhansk Oblast
summary: Luhansk Oblast is the easternmost province of Ukraine, with its administrative center in the city of [[luhansk|Luhansk]]. Established in 1938, the oblast has been significantly affected by conflict, particularly since the 2014 pro-Russian insurgency and the ongoing Russian invasion that began in 2022.

title: Luhansk People's Republic
summary: The Luhansk People's Republic (LPR) is a self-proclaimed republic in eastern Ukraine, established in 2014 amid pro-Russian unrest and conflict. It has been characterized as a disputed territory, often regarded as a puppet state of Russia, and was unilaterally annexed by Russia in 2022.

title: Lutsk
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Lutsk is a city located on the Styr River in northwestern Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Volyn Oblast and Lutsk Raion. With a population of 220,986 as of 2022, Lutsk boasts a rich history dating back to its first mention in 1085, playing a significant role as an administrative, cultural, and religious hub in the region of Volhynia.

title: Lutsk Raion
summary: Lutsk Raion is a district located in Volyn Oblast, [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], with its administrative center in the city of Lutsk. As of 2022, the population of the raion is 457,287, following significant administrative reforms in 2020 that expanded its area.

title: Lviv
summary: Lviv is the fifth-largest city [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] and the largest in the western region, with an estimated population of 723,403 in 2025. It serves as the administrative center of [[lviv-oblast|Lviv Oblast]] and is recognized as a key cultural hub in Ukraine.

title: Lviv City Council
summary: The Lviv City Council is the governing body of Lviv, a prominent city [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], with a structure comprising 64 elected representatives serving five-year terms.

title: Lviv High Castle
summary: The Lviv High Castle, known in Ukrainian as Високий замок, is a historic castle situated on Castle Hill in Lviv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. It is the highest point in the city, standing at 413 metres (1,355 ft) above sea level, and currently exists in a state of ruin.

title: Lviv National Academy of Arts
summary: The Lviv National Academy of Arts is a prominent higher education institution located in Lviv, Ukraine, known for its significant contributions to the fields of fine arts and design.
aliases: Lviv State Institute of Applied and Decorative Art

title: Lviv National Environmental University
summary: Lviv National Environmental University is a prominent [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] institution located in Dubliany, near Lviv, with a rich history dating back to 1852. It has evolved through various educational phases, reflecting the agricultural and environmental focus of the region.

title: Lviv National Museum
summary: The Andrey Sheptytsky National Museum of Lviv is one of the largest museums [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], dedicated to showcasing the country's cultural heritage. Established in 1905 by Metropolitan Archbishop Andrey Sheptytsky, the museum has evolved significantly over the years, housing an extensive collection of Ukrainian art and artifacts.

title: Lviv Oblast
summary: Lviv Oblast is an administrative region in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], centered around the city of Lviv, with a population estimated at 2,478,133 in 2022. The oblast is significant for its rich history, diverse geography, and cultural heritage, reflecting the region's complex past and its role in contemporary Ukraine.

title: Lviv Polytechnic
summary: Lviv Polytechnic National University is a prominent public university located in Lviv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], established in 1816. It holds a significant position in the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] higher education system, ranking first among technical institutions and second overall as of 2024.

title: Lviv Theatre of Opera and Ballet
summary: The Solomiya Krushelnytska Lviv State Academic Theatre of Opera and Ballet, commonly known as Lviv Opera, is a prominent opera house in Lviv, Ukraine. Designed by Polish architect Zygmunt Gorgolewski, it serves as a significant cultural institution in the region, reflecting the historical and artistic heritage of Ukraine.
aliases: Solomiya Krushelnytska Lviv State Academic Theatre of Opera and Ballet

title: Lviv University
summary: The Ivan Franko National University of Lviv is a state-sponsored institution located in Lviv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], and is recognized as the oldest university in continuous operation in [[modern-history-of-ukraine|modern Ukraine]], established in 1661. Named after the prominent Ukrainian poet Ivan Franko since 1940, the university has played a significant role in the educational and cultural landscape of Ukraine.
aliases: Ivan Franko National University of Lviv

title: Lysychansk
summary: Lysychansk is a city located in Sievierodonetsk Raion, Luhansk Oblast, in eastern [[ukraine|Ukraine]], situated on the right bank of the Donets River. Historically significant as a mining and industrial center, it has faced considerable challenges, particularly during the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.

title: Maidan Nezalezhnosti
summary: Maidan Nezalezhnosti, or Independence Square, is the central square of Kyiv, Ukraine, significant for its role in political movements and as a symbol of [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] independence. It features the Independence Monument and has been the site of numerous historic protests and events since the 1990s.

title: Makariv
summary: Makariv is an urban-type settlement located in Bucha Raion of Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of the Makariv settlement hromada. As of 2022, it has a population of 9,390, reflecting a decline from 12,042 in 2001.

title: Makiivka
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Makiivka is an industrial city located in [[donetsk-oblast|Donetsk Oblast]], eastern [[ukraine|Ukraine]], with a significant history of coal mining and metallurgy. As of 2022, it has an estimated population of 338,968 and is currently under Russian occupation following the conflict in the Donbas region.

title: Maksym Kryvonis
summary: Maksym Kryvonis was a prominent Cossack leader and military commander during the Khmelnytskyi Uprising against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, notable for his strategic victories and controversial actions against Jewish communities.

title: Mariinskyi Park
summary: Mariinskyi Park is a historic park located in the Pechersk neighborhood of Kyiv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], serving both as a recreational area and a Soviet necropolis. Established in 1874, it has undergone various transformations and is recognized as part of Ukraine's Nature Preservation Fund.

title: Marina Abramović
summary: Marina Abramović is a Serbian conceptual and performance artist known for her exploration of body art, endurance, and the interaction between performer and audience. Active for over four decades, she has been recognized as a pivotal figure in contemporary performance art, significantly influencing the field and its practices.

title: Mariupol
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Mariupol is a city of regional significance located in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine, on the northern coast of the Sea of Azov. Historically an industrial and trade center, it has faced significant challenges, particularly during the [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|Russo-Ukrainian War]].

title: Mariupol theatre airstrike
summary: The Mariupol theatre airstrike occurred on 16 March 2022 during the Russian [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|invasion of Ukraine]], targeting a building used as an air raid shelter for civilians. This attack has been classified as a war crime by various organizations due to the high number of civilian casualties and the deliberate nature of the bombing.

title: Maslenitsa
summary: Maslenitsa, also known as Butter Lady or Cheesefare Week, is an Eastern Slavic holiday celebrated in Ukraine and other Slavic countries during the last week before Great Lent. This festival retains elements of Slavic mythology and is characterized by various traditional activities and culinary practices.

title: matryoshka doll
summary: The matryoshka doll, also known as a Russian nesting doll, is a traditional wooden doll set originating from Russia, consisting of decreasingly sized figures placed one inside another. This cultural artifact is significant in Ukraine, reflecting shared Slavic heritage and artistic expression.

title: Mavka
summary: Mavka, or Nyavka, is a class of female spirit in Ukrainian folklore, often depicted as a beautiful temptress associated with the forest. These entities are believed to represent the souls of girls who died tragically, luring men to their demise while also having roles in agricultural life.

title: Mavka: The Forest Song
summary: Mavka: The Forest Song is a 3D-animated fantasy film from [[ukraine|Ukraine]], released in 2023, that draws inspiration from Lesya Ukrainka's play of the same name. The film, produced by the Animagrad studio under The Film.UA Group, showcases characters from Ukrainian and Slavic folklore and has achieved significant recognition in the realm of independent Ukrainian cinema.

title: Melitopol
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Melitopol is a significant city and municipality located in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, southeastern [[ukraine|Ukraine]], known for its strategic location and historical importance. As of January 2022, it had a population of approximately 148,851 and has been under Russian control since March 2022, although it remains internationally recognized as part of Ukraine.

title: Memorial in Commemoration of Famines' Victims in Ukraine
summary: The National Museum of the Holodomor-Genocide serves as Ukraine's [[lviv-national-museum|national museum]] dedicated to the victims of the Holodomor, a man-made famine that resulted in millions of deaths in Ukraine during 1932–1933. Established in 2008 and recognized as a national museum in 2010, it aims to preserve the memory of the Holodomor and educate future generations.

title: Metinvest
summary: Metinvest is a prominent group of steel and mining companies with significant operations in Ukraine and other countries. It is recognized as Ukraine's largest producer of iron ore and steel, playing a vital role in the nation's economy.

title: Mezhyhirya
summary: Mezhyhirya is an estate [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] that served as the residence of Viktor Yanukovych during his tenure as Prime Minister and President. It has since become a museum that reflects Yanukovych's opulent lifestyle and the controversies surrounding his administration.

title: Mikhail Bulgakov
summary: Mikhail Bulgakov was a prominent Russian and Soviet novelist and playwright, born in Kiev, which is now the capital of Ukraine. His notable works include The Master and Margarita and The White Guard, the latter reflecting his experiences during the turbulent times in Ukraine and Russia.

title: Mikhail Gorbachev
summary: Mikhail Sergeyevich Gorbachev (2 March 1931 – 30 August 2022) was a prominent Soviet and Russian politician, serving as the last leader of the Soviet Union from 1985 until its dissolution in 1991. His policies of reform had significant implications for Ukraine, particularly in the context of the Soviet Union's eventual collapse.

title: Mikhail Kovalchuk
summary: Mikhail Valentinovich Kovalchuk is a Russian physicist and official, born on September 21, 1946. He is notably the brother of Yury Kovalchuk, who is recognized as a significant financial figure within the Russian political landscape.

title: Mikhail Lomonosov
summary: Mikhail Vasilyevich Lomonosov (19 November 1711 – 15 April 1765) was a prominent Russian polymath whose extensive contributions spanned literature, science, and education, significantly impacting the intellectual landscape of [[ukraine|Ukraine]] and Russia. He is recognized for his discoveries in various scientific fields, including chemistry and astronomy, and is often regarded as the 'Father of Russian Science.'

title: Ministry of Defence of Ukraine
summary: The Ministry of Defence of Ukraine is the governmental body responsible for overseeing national defense and the Armed Forces of Ukraine. Established on 24 September 1991, it plays a crucial role in military organization, strategic planning, and international military cooperation.

title: Ministry of Economy
summary: The Ministry for Development of Economy and Trade of Ukraine is the primary governmental authority responsible for formulating and implementing economic and social development policies in the country. It plays a crucial role in regulating various economic sectors and coordinating Ukraine's economic relations with the European Union.

title: Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine
summary: The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is the principal executive authority responsible for education and scientific development [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]. Established in its modern form in 1992, the ministry has undergone various reorganizations and plays a crucial role in shaping the educational landscape of the country.

title: Ministry of Finance of Ukraine
summary: The Ministry of Finance of Ukraine is a key governmental body responsible for formulating and executing national financial and budgetary policies, as well as overseeing customs and taxation regulations [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]. Its functions are vital for ensuring the state's financial stability and promoting economic growth.

title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine
summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine is the governmental body responsible for managing Ukraine's foreign relations. It plays a crucial role in shaping Ukraine's diplomatic policies and international presence.

title: Ministry of Infrastructure of Ukraine
summary: The Ministry of Infrastructure of Ukraine serves as the primary executive authority overseeing the nation's transportation infrastructure, including roads, railways, and communications, as well as tourism policy implementation.

title: Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine
summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine is a governmental body responsible for overseeing the country's internal affairs, including law enforcement and civil security. Established in its current form in 1991, it has undergone significant reforms, particularly following the Euromaidan protests in 2015.
aliases: Ministry of the Interior of Ukraine

title: Ministry of Justice of Ukraine
summary: The Ministry of Justice of Ukraine is the principal governmental body responsible for regulating the state's legal policy and ensuring the protection of human rights within Ukraine. Established in the early 20th century, it plays a crucial role in aligning Ukrainian legislation with European Union standards.

title: minorities in Ukraine
type: groups of people in a location
summary: Minorities in Ukraine constitute 22.2 percent of the nation's population, featuring a diverse array of ethnic groups. The presence of these minorities is significant in the context of Ukraine's cultural landscape and its relations with neighboring countries.

title: Minsk agreements
summary: The Minsk agreements were a series of international accords aimed at resolving the conflict in Eastern Ukraine, specifically the Donbas War, which involved armed Russian separatists and the [[armed-forces-of-ukraine|Armed Forces of Ukraine]]. The agreements, known as Minsk I and Minsk II, sought to establish ceasefires and outline steps for peace, but faced numerous violations and challenges, significantly impacting Ukraine's territorial integrity and security.

title: modern history of Ukraine
summary: The modern history of Ukraine is marked by its evolution from a region under imperial control to an independent nation-state, characterized by significant events such as the Ukrainian National Revival, the struggle for independence, Soviet rule, and ongoing conflicts in the post-Soviet era.

title: Moldova–Ukraine relations
summary: Moldova–Ukraine relations encompass the diplomatic ties between Moldova and Ukraine, two former Soviet republics that share a 985-kilometer border. The relationship is significant due to the presence of a substantial Ukrainian minority in Moldova and both nations' aspirations for European Union membership.

title: Molodist Kyiv International Film Festival
summary: The Molodist Kyiv International Film Festival is a prominent film festival held annually in October in Kyiv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. Established in 1970, it has grown to become the largest film festival in the country, showcasing a diverse array of films and supporting the development of young filmmakers.

title: Moskva
summary: Moskva, previously known as Slava, was a guided missile cruiser of the Russian Navy, commissioned in 1983 and serving as the flagship of the Black Sea Fleet. Its involvement in the [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|Russo-Ukrainian War]], particularly during the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, marked a significant chapter in its operational history.

title: Mother Ukraine Monument
summary: The Mother Ukraine Monument is a monumental statue located in Kyiv, Ukraine, symbolizing the nation's resilience and history. Originally constructed during the Soviet era, the monument has undergone significant changes, particularly in response to contemporary geopolitical events.

title: Motor Sich
summary: Motor Sich, Joint Stock Company, is a prominent Ukrainian aircraft engine manufacturer located in Zaporizhzhia, specializing in engines for airplanes, helicopters, and industrial marine gas turbines.

title: Mukachevo
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Mukachevo is a city of regional significance located in [[zakarpattia-oblast|Zakarpattia Oblast]], [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of Mukachevo Raion. Historically significant and ethnically diverse, it has a rich cultural heritage and plays a vital role in the region's economy and demographics.

title: Museum of the Great Patriotic War
summary: The Museum of the Great Patriotic War refers to various history museums established in [[soviet-union|the Soviet Union]], focusing on the Eastern Front during World War II, with significant relevance to [[ukraine|Ukraine]]'s historical narrative.

title: music of Ukraine
summary: The music of Ukraine encompasses a rich tapestry of influences from both Western and Eastern European traditions, deeply rooted in indigenous Slavic and Christian elements. It reflects the country's historical significance as a cultural hub within the former Russian Empire and showcases a diverse array of folk and classical music forms.

title: Mykhailo Hrushevskyi
summary: Mykhailo Hrushevskyi was a prominent Ukrainian historian, politician, and statesman, recognized as a key figure in the [[ukrainian-national-revival|Ukrainian national revival]] of the early 20th century. His contributions to Ukrainian history and culture, particularly through his extensive writings and political activism, have left a lasting impact on Ukraine's national identity.

title: Mykola Azarov
summary: Mykola Yanovych Azarov is a notable Russo-Ukrainian politician who served as the [[prime-minister-of-ukraine|Prime Minister of Ukraine]] from 11 March 2010 to 27 January 2014. His political career is marked by significant roles in the [[cabinet-of-ministers-of-ukraine|Ukrainian government]] and his controversial actions during the Euromaidan protests.

title: Mykola Hlushchenko
summary: Mykola Hlushchenko was a prominent Ukrainian artist known for his contributions to the art world and his recognition with the Shevchenko National Prize in 1972. His work and influence span several countries, reflecting a deep connection to Ukrainian culture and history.

title: Mykola Hrinchenko
summary: Mykola Volodymyrovych Hrinchenko is a retired Ukrainian professional football midfielder, born on 27 February 1986.

title: Mykola Leontovych
summary: Mykola Dmytrovych Leontovych was a prominent Ukrainian composer, conductor, ethnomusicologist, and educator, known for his significant contributions to choral music and folk arrangements. His most famous work, 'Shchedryk', has become a staple in both Ukrainian and global musical repertoires.

title: Mykola Lysenko
summary: Mykola Vitaliiovych Lysenko was a prominent Ukrainian composer, pianist, conductor, and ethnomusicologist, born on 22 March 1842 and passing on 6 November 1912. He played a crucial role in establishing a national music tradition [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] during the late Romantic period, influencing future generations of Ukrainian musicians.

title: Mykola Shchors
summary: Mykola Oleksandrovych Shchors was a Ukrainian-born commander in the Red Army during the Russian Civil War, known for his role in the conflict against the Ukrainian People's Republic. His legacy has been shaped by both his military actions and the subsequent glorification of his image in Soviet culture.

title: Mykola Voronyi
summary: Mykola Voronyi was a prominent Ukrainian writer, poet, actor, director, and political activist, whose contributions significantly influenced Ukrainian literature and theatre in the early 20th century.

title: Mykolaiv
summary: Mykolaiv is a significant port city and administrative center in southern Ukraine, known for its strategic location at the confluence of the Inhul and Southern Bug rivers. It is recognized as a key shipbuilding hub and has been impacted by historical events, including the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

title: Mykolaiv Oblast
summary: Mykolaiv Oblast is a province in southern Ukraine, with its administrative center located in the city of Mykolaiv. As of 2022, the oblast has a population of approximately 1,091,821 residents and is significant for its historical, geographical, and economic contributions to Ukraine.

title: Mykolaiv Raion
summary: Mykolaiv Raion is a district located in Mykolaiv Oblast, Ukraine, with a pre-war population estimated at 636,832 in 2022. The administrative center of the raion is the city of Mykolaiv.

title: Mykolaiv Shipyard
summary: Mykolaiv Shipyard refers to several shipbuilding facilities located in the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] city of Mykolaiv, which is significant for its maritime industry.

title: Mykolayiv State Agrarian University
summary: Mykolaiv National Agrarian University (MNAU) is a prominent public agricultural college located in Mykolaiv, Ukraine, recognized for its contributions to agrarian education and research.

title: Myrhorod
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Myrhorod is a city of regional significance located in [[poltava-oblast|Poltava Oblast]], central Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Myrhorod Raion and hosting the Myrhorod urban hromada. The city, situated on the Khorol River, had an estimated population of 37,886 in 2022.

title: Myroslav Skoryk
summary: Myroslav Mykhailovych Skoryk (13 July 1938 – 1 June 2020) was a prominent Ukrainian composer and educator known for his contemporary musical style that incorporates elements of Ukrainian folk traditions. He received significant national honors, including the titles of People's Artist of Ukraine and Hero of Ukraine.

title: Nadia
summary: Nadia is a female given name with various linguistic variations, notably in Slavic languages where it signifies 'hope'. The name has significant cultural relevance in Ukraine, where the Ukrainian variant is Nadiya (Надія).

title: Nadiya Savchenko
summary: Nadiya Savchenko is a prominent Ukrainian politician and former Army aviation pilot known for her significant role during the War in Donbas and her subsequent imprisonment in Russia. She has been a symbol of Ukraine's struggle for sovereignty and human rights.

title: Nafpaktos
summary: Nafpaktos is a town located in the Nafpaktia region of Aetolia-Acarnania in West Greece, historically significant for its strategic maritime position and its connection to various military conflicts, including the Battle of Lepanto. The town's rich history and cultural heritage are relevant to understanding the broader historical context of the Mediterranean, including its interactions with [[history-of-ukraine|Ukrainian history]] through trade and military alliances.

title: Naftogaz of Ukraine
summary: Naftogaz of Ukraine is the largest state-owned oil and gas company in Ukraine, responsible for the complete cycle of natural gas and crude oil operations. The company plays a crucial role in Ukraine's energy sector and has significant influence in regional politics due to its infrastructure connecting Russia and the European Union.

title: National Academy of Arts of Ukraine
summary: The National Academy of Arts of Ukraine (NAA) is a prominent national institution dedicated to the arts, established in 1996 and granted national status in 2010. It plays a vital role in promoting and preserving Ukrainian artistic traditions and culture both domestically and internationally.

title: National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine
summary: The National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine (NASU) is a self-governing, state-funded organization that serves as the primary hub for scientific and technological development in Ukraine, coordinating a network of research institutes across the country. Established in 1918, it has played a significant role in the advancement of various scientific disciplines within the Ukrainian context.

title: National Art Museum of Ukraine
summary: The National Art Museum of Ukraine, located in Kyiv, is a prominent institution dedicated to the preservation and exhibition of Ukrainian art. Established at the end of the 19th century, it houses an extensive collection that spans from [[kievan-rus|Kievan Rus]]' to contemporary works.

title: National Ballet of Ukraine
summary: The National Ballet of Ukraine, associated with the [[taras-shevchenko|Taras Shevchenko]] National Opera of Ukraine, is a prominent ballet company known for its classical performances and international tours. With a repertory of 24 ballets, it is one of the largest ballet companies globally and has a rich history intertwined with Ukraine's cultural development.

title: National Bank of Ukraine
summary: The National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) serves as the central bank of Ukraine, established in 1991 from the Soviet Gosbank's Ukrainian operations. It plays a crucial role in regulating the country's financial system and ensuring the stability of the national currency, the Hryvnia.

title: National Forestry University
summary: The National Forestry and Wood-Technology University of Ukraine is a prominent educational institution located in Lviv, specializing in forestry and wood technology. It has a rich historical background that reflects the evolution of forestry [[education-in-ukraine|education in Ukraine]].

title: National Guard of Ukraine
summary: The National Guard of Ukraine (NGU) serves as the national gendarmerie and internal troops, operating under the [[ministry-of-internal-affairs-of-ukraine|Ministry of Internal Affairs]] to maintain public security and support state defense. Established on November 4, 1991, it has undergone significant transformations, particularly in response to national crises, including the 2014 [[revolution-of-dignity|Revolution of Dignity]] and the ongoing Russo-Ukrainian War.

title: National Historical Museum of Ukraine
summary: The National Museum of the History of Ukraine, known as MIST, is a prominent institution that showcases the historical narrative of Ukraine from ancient times to the present. With a collection of approximately 800,000 items, it plays a vital role in preserving and presenting Ukrainian heritage.
aliases: National Museum of the History of Ukraine

title: National Museum of Literature of Ukraine
summary: The National Museum of Literature of Ukraine is a prominent institution located in Kyiv, dedicated to the evolution of Ukrainian literature from the 9th century to the present. It serves as a vital cultural repository, showcasing the contributions of notable Ukrainian authors and the historical significance of literature in the nation.

title: National Museum of Natural History
summary: The National Museum of Natural History (NMNH) is a prominent natural history museum located in Washington, D.C., administered by the Smithsonian Institution. It houses the largest natural history collection in the world, with over 148 million specimens, and serves as a vital resource for research and education, including connections to [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] natural history and cultural studies.

summary: The National Museum of the History of Ukraine in World War II is a significant memorial complex located in Kyiv, dedicated to commemorating the German-Soviet War. It is notable for its extensive collection and the iconic Mother Ukraine monument, reflecting Ukraine's historical narrative and evolving identity.

title: National Museum Тaras Shevchenko
summary: The National Museum of Taras Shevchenko, located in Kyiv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], is dedicated to the life and contributions of the prominent Ukrainian painter and national poet, Taras Shevchenko.

title: National Opera of Ukraine
summary: The National Opera of Ukraine, established in 1867, is the second oldest opera company in the country, performing at the Kyiv Opera House named after Taras Shevchenko. It has played a significant role in the cultural landscape of Ukraine, showcasing both Ukrainian and international operatic works.

title: National Philharmonic of Ukraine
summary: The National Philharmonic of Ukraine, located in Kyiv, is a prominent cultural institution known for its concert halls and rich musical heritage. Established through the efforts of [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] composer Mykola Lysenko, it has played a significant role in the promotion of both Ukrainian and international music.

title: National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine
summary: The National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine (NSDCU) is a key governmental agency responsible for coordinating national security and defense policies under the President of Ukraine. Established in 1991, it has evolved to play a significant role in shaping Ukraine's security landscape, particularly since 2014.

title: National University of Kyiv-Mohyla Academy
summary: The National University of Kyiv-Mohyla Academy (NaUKMA) is a prominent research university located in Kyiv, Ukraine, known for its bilingual education and international collaborations. Established in 1991, it traces its roots to the historic Kyiv-Mohyla Academy founded in 1615, which played a significant role in the intellectual development of Ukraine and Eastern Europe.

summary: The National University of Physical Education and Sport of Ukraine, located in Kyiv, is a prominent institution dedicated to the fields of physical education and sports [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

title: Natural gas in Ukraine
summary: Natural gas plays a crucial role [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s energy landscape, with significant domestic production, consumption, and a vast transmission system. Ukraine is notable for having the largest gas storage capacity in Europe, which is vital for meeting seasonal demand.

title: Nestor the Chronicler
summary: Nestor the Chronicler (c. 1056 – c. 1114) was a monk at the Monastery of the Caves in Kiev, recognized for his significant contributions to [[kievan-rus|Kievan Rus]]' literature, particularly through his hagiographies. His works, including the Life of the Venerable Theodosius and the Account of Boris and Gleb, are vital to understanding the cultural and religious [[history-of-ukraine|history of Ukraine]].

title: Nikita Khrushchev
summary: Nikita Sergeyevich Khrushchev was a prominent Soviet leader, serving as First Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union from 1953 to 1964 and Chairman of the Council of Ministers from 1958 to 1964. His political career was marked by significant events such as the denunciation of Joseph Stalin and the Cuban Missile Crisis, with deep connections to Ukraine throughout his life.

title: Nikolai Gogol
summary: Nikolai Vasilyevich Gogol (1 April [O.S. 20 March] 1809 – 4 March [O.S. 21 February] 1852) was a prominent novelist, short-story writer, and playwright with Ukrainian roots, whose works have significantly influenced both Russian and [[ukrainian-literature|Ukrainian literature]].

title: Nikolay Aleksandrovich Tikhonov
summary: Nikolay Aleksandrovich Tikhonov was a prominent Soviet Russian-Ukrainian statesman who played a significant role during the Cold War, particularly as Chairman of the Council of Ministers from 1980 to 1985. His political career began [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], and he was influential in the economic and cultural administration of [[soviet-union|the Soviet Union]] during a period of stagnation.

title: Nina Matviienko
summary: Nina Mytrofanivna Matviienko was a prominent Ukrainian singer, born on 10 October 1947 and passing away on 8 October 2023. She was renowned for her contributions to [[ukrainian-folk-music|Ukrainian folk music]] and her performances that celebrated the cultural heritage of Ukraine.

title: Nizhyn
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Nizhyn is a city of regional significance located in Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine, along the Oster River. As of 2022, it has a population of 65,830 and serves as the administrative center of Nizhyn Raion, highlighting its importance within the region.

title: Nova Post
summary: Nova Poshta, known as Nova Post outside Ukraine, is a private postal and courier service based in Ukraine, providing logistics solutions for both individuals and businesses. Established in 2001, it has grown to become a significant player in the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] market, competing primarily with Ukrposhta.

title: Novomoskovsk
summary: Novomoskovsk refers to several locations and entities, primarily highlighting the town [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s Dnipropetrovsk Oblast and its historical significance.

title: nuclear power in Ukraine
summary: Nuclear power plays a significant role in Ukraine's energy landscape, with four nuclear power plants, including the largest in Europe, the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant. Despite challenges, including occupation and conflict, Ukraine continues to rely heavily on nuclear energy for electricity generation.

title: Odesa
summary: Odesa, a significant port city in Ukraine, is the third-most populous municipality in the country and serves as a vital transport hub on the Black Sea. Its rich history, multicultural heritage, and recent recognition as a World Heritage Site underscore its importance in the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] context.

title: Odesa Catacombs
summary: The Odesa Catacombs are an extensive network of tunnels beneath the city of Odesa, Ukraine, primarily formed through stone mining. This labyrinth, which reaches depths of 60 metres and spans approximately 2,500 kilometres, has historical significance, having served various purposes from construction to wartime shelters.

title: Odesa Film Studio
summary: Odesa Film Studio is a prominent Ukrainian film studio located in Odesa, [[odesa-oblast|Odesa Oblast]], with a history dating back to its founding in 1919. It is one of the oldest film studios in the region and plays a significant role in the Ukrainian film industry.

title: Odesa International Airport
summary: Odesa International Airport is an international airport located in Odesa, Ukraine's third largest city, approximately 7 km southwest of the city center. It has been significantly impacted by the ongoing Russo-Ukrainian War, particularly since the closure of airspace to civilian flights on 24 February 2022.

title: Odesa International Film Festival
summary: The Odesa International Film Festival is an annual film festival held in Odesa, Ukraine, each July since its inception in 2010. It features a variety of competitions and programs showcasing both international and national films, emphasizing the festival's significance in promoting Ukrainian cinema.

title: Odesa National Maritime University
summary: Odesa National Maritime University is a public institution located in Odesa, Ukraine, specializing in maritime education. Established in 1930, it has educated students from more than 90 countries in fields pertinent to the maritime industry.

title: Odesa Oblast
summary: Odesa Oblast is a province in southwestern Ukraine, situated along the northern coast of the Black Sea, with Odesa as its administrative center. As of 2022, the population is estimated at 2,351,382, and the region is notable for its extensive coastline, significant agricultural production, and rich historical heritage.

title: Oksana Baiul
summary: Oksana Serhiyivna Baiul-Farina is a retired [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] figure skater, celebrated for winning the gold medal in ladies' singles at the 1994 Winter Olympics and the 1993 World Championship. She is recognized as the first Olympic champion from [[ukraine|Ukraine]] to compete under the [[flag-of-ukraine|Ukrainian flag]] and is a significant figure in the history of Ukrainian sports.

title: Oksana Lyniv
summary: Oksana Yaroslavivna Lyniv is a prominent [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] conductor known for her groundbreaking achievements in the field of classical music. She serves as the music director of the Teatro Comunale di Bologna and has significantly contributed to the establishment of the Youth Symphony Orchestra of Ukraine.

title: Oksana Zabuzhko
summary: Oksana Stefanivna Zabuzhko is a prominent Ukrainian novelist, poet, and essayist born on 19 September 1960 in Lutsk, Ukraine. Her literary contributions, particularly in exploring national identity and gender, have positioned her as a key figure in contemporary Ukrainian literature.

title: Oleh Blokhin
summary: Oleh Blokhin is a prominent Ukrainian former football player and manager, celebrated as one of the greatest footballers of his generation. He holds numerous records in Ukrainian and Soviet football, including being the all-time top goalscorer for both Dynamo Kyiv and the Soviet Union national team.

title: Oleh Liashko
summary: Oleh Valeriiovych Liashko is a Ukrainian politician, journalist, and soldier known for his long tenure in the Verkhovna Rada and as the leader of the Radical Party. He has played a significant role in Ukrainian politics, particularly during times of conflict.

title: Oleh Sentsov
summary: Oleh Sentsov is a Ukrainian filmmaker, writer, activist, and soldier from Crimea, known for his opposition to the [[russian-annexation-of-crimea|Russian annexation of Crimea]] and his subsequent imprisonment by Russian authorities. He has actively participated [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s military efforts following the 2022 invasion by Russia.

title: Oleh Skrypka
summary: Oleh Yuriyovych Skrypka is a prominent Ukrainian musician, vocalist, composer, and leader of the rock group Vopli Vidoplyasova, known for his significant contributions to the [[music-of-ukraine|Ukrainian music]] scene and cultural identity.

title: Oleksandr Dovzhenko
summary: Oleksandr Dovzhenko was a prominent Soviet film director and screenwriter of Ukrainian descent, recognized as a key figure in early Soviet cinema and a pioneer of montage theory. His works, particularly the 'Ukraine Trilogy,' reflect the cultural and historical narratives of Ukraine during the early 20th century.

title: Oleksandr Turchynov
summary: Oleksandr Turchynov is a prominent Ukrainian politician, economist, and Baptist minister, known for his roles in the [[cabinet-of-ministers-of-ukraine|Ukrainian government]], including serving as acting President and Secretary of the National Security and Defence Council. His political career has been significantly intertwined with key events in Ukraine's recent history, particularly during the 2014 political crisis and the ongoing conflict with Russia.

title: Oleksandr Vysotskyi
summary: Oleksandr Oleksandrovych Vysotskyi is a former professional football goalkeeper from [[ukraine|Ukraine]], born on 16 June 1986. His career in football reflects the sporting culture and talent development within Ukraine.

title: Oles Honchar
summary: Oleksandr 'Oles' Terentiiovych Honchar was a prominent Soviet and Ukrainian writer, public figure, and World War II veteran, known for his significant contributions to [[ukrainian-literature|Ukrainian literature]] and his involvement in political life. He was born on April 3, 1918, and passed away on July 14, 1995.

title: Oles Honchar Dnipro National University
summary: Oles Honchar Dnipro National University (DNU) is a prominent state-sponsored educational institution in Dnipro, Ukraine, founded in 1918. It serves as a significant center for higher education and research, offering a wide range of programs and maintaining strong connections with international academic institutions.

title: Oleshky Sands
summary: Oleshky Sands is a semi-desert region located [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], characterized by sand dunes known as kuchuhury, which can reach heights of up to five meters. This area is significant for its unique ecosystem and historical context within Kherson Oblast.

title: Olesko
summary: Olesko is a rural settlement located in Zolochiv Raion of Lviv Oblast in western Ukraine, with a population of 1,418 as of 2022. It is part of the Busk urban hromada, reflecting its integration into the administrative structure of [[ukraine|Ukraine]].

title: Olesko Castle
summary: Olesko Castle, located in present-day Zolochiv Raion, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], is a historically significant structure with roots dating back to the 14th century. It is renowned for its association with notable figures in Polish and [[history-of-ukraine|Ukrainian history]] and serves as a museum today.

title: Olga Kurylenko
summary: Olga Kostyantynivna Kurylenko is a Ukrainian-French actress and former model, known for her role as Camille Montes in the James Bond film Quantum of Solace (2008). Born in Berdyansk, Ukraine, she has gained international recognition through her diverse filmography and significant contributions to cinema.

title: Operation Barbarossa
summary: Operation Barbarossa was the code name for the Nazi Germany invasion of the Soviet Union, commencing on 22 June 1941, which significantly impacted Ukraine and its territories. This operation marked a pivotal escalation in World War II, leading to extensive military engagements and profound humanitarian crises in the region.

title: Operation Vistula
summary: Operation Vistula was a military operation conducted in 1947 that involved the ethnic cleansing, deportation, and forced resettlement of nearly 150,000 Ukrainians, [[rusyns|Rusyns]], Boykos, and Lemkos from southeastern Poland to the northern and western territories of the country. This operation aimed to suppress the Ukrainian Insurgent Army and significantly impacted the Ukrainian population in Poland.

title: Orange Revolution
summary: The Orange Revolution was a series of protests in Ukraine from late November 2004 to January 2005, initiated by widespread public discontent over perceived electoral fraud in the presidential election. The movement ultimately led to the annulment of the election results and a re-vote, resulting in Viktor Yushchenko's presidency.

title: Orel
summary: Orel refers to various geographical locations, vehicles, and cultural references, with notable connections to Ukraine through the Oril river.

title: Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists
summary: The Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN) was a significant Ukrainian nationalist group founded on February 2, 1929, in Vienna, which played a crucial role in the political landscape of [[ukraine|Ukraine]] during the interwar period and World War II. The OUN aimed to establish an ethnically homogeneous Ukrainian state through radical nationalist ideologies and violent tactics.

title: Oschadbank
summary: Oschadbank, officially known as Public JSC 'State Savings Bank of Ukraine', is a significant public bank in Ukraine recognized as one of the country's systemically important banks. Established after the dissolution of the Soviet Union, Oschadbank plays a crucial role in the Ukrainian banking sector, providing various financial services across its extensive branch and ATM network.

title: Ostap Bender
summary: Ostap Bender is a fictional character created by Soviet authors Ilya Ilf and Yevgeny Petrov, serving as the central antihero in the novels The Twelve Chairs (1928) and The Little Golden Calf (1931). His character, originating from Odesa, embodies themes of entrepreneurship and satire relevant to the socio-economic landscape of [[ukraine|Ukraine]] and the Soviet Union.

title: Ostrih Bible
summary: The Ostrog Bible, published in 1581 in Ostrog, Ukraine, was the first complete printed edition of the Bible in Church Slavonic. Commissioned by Konstanty Wasyl Ostrogski and printed by Ivan Fyodorov, it played a crucial role in the development of Orthodox education in the region.

title: Ostriv
summary: Ostriv, meaning 'island' in [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]], refers to various locations within Ukraine and a video game. The term encompasses multiple places across several Ukrainian oblasts.

title: Ostroh Academy
summary: Ostroh Academy, founded in 1576 by Konstanty Wasyl Ostrogski, was a significant educational institution in Ostroh, within the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth. Recognized as the first higher education establishment in the Eastern Slavic world, it played a crucial role in the Orthodox cultural revival known as the 'Ostroh Renaissance' and was instrumental in the publication of the Ostroh Bible in 1581.

title: Pale of Settlement
summary: The Pale of Settlement was a designated area within the Russian Empire from 1791 to 1917, where permanent residency for Jewish individuals was permitted. This region included significant parts of modern-day Ukraine and was characterized by restrictive laws and economic challenges for its Jewish inhabitants.

title: Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe
summary: The Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) serves as the parliamentary component of the Council of Europe, comprising 46 member states and focusing on human rights, democracy, and the rule of law. Its relevance to Ukraine is underscored by its actions and resolutions regarding human rights and democratic governance, particularly in the context of the ongoing conflict with Russia.

title: paska
summary: Paska is a traditional Ukrainian Easter bread that holds cultural significance in Ukraine and other Central and Eastern European countries with ties to the Byzantine Empire and Eastern Christianity. It is an essential part of Easter celebrations, symbolizing the resurrection of Christ and featuring prominently in various festive customs.

title: Pavlivka

title: Pavlo Klimkin
summary: Pavlo Klimkin is a prominent Ukrainian diplomat who served as the Minister of Foreign Affairs from June 19, 2014, to August 29, 2019. His diplomatic career has significantly influenced Ukraine's foreign relations, particularly in the context of European integration and negotiations with Russia.

title: Pavlo Skoropadsky
summary: Pavlo Petrovych Skoropadsky was a prominent Ukrainian aristocrat, military leader, and statesman who served as the hetman of the [[ukrainian-state|Ukrainian State]] in 1918. His leadership was marked by significant political and military developments during a tumultuous period in [[history-of-ukraine|Ukrainian history]].

title: Pavlo Tychyna
summary: Pavlo Hryhorovych Tychyna was a prominent Ukrainian poet, translator, publicist, and statesman, born on January 23, 1891, in Pisky, Ukraine. He is best known for composing the lyrics of the Anthem of the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic and for his complex relationship with the Soviet regime.

title: Pavlo Tychyna Museum
summary: The Pavlo Tychyna Museum, officially known as the Literary and Memorial Museum of Pavlo Tychyna, is located in [[kyiv|Kyiv]], [[ukraine|Ukraine]], and is dedicated to the life and works of the Ukrainian writer [[pavlo-tychyna|Pavlo Tychyna]].

title: Pavlo Zibrov
summary: Pavlo Mykolaiovich Zibrov is a prominent Ukrainian pop singer and songwriter, recognized as a People's Artist of Ukraine since 1996. He is particularly known for his collaboration on the song 'Khreshchatyk' with Yuriy Rybchynskyi.

title: Pavlohrad

summary: Pavlohrad is a city in eastern Ukraine, situated in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, and serves as the administrative center of Pavlohrad Raion. As of 2022, the city has an estimated population of approximately 101,430.

title: Pavlovo
