While the name is prevalent in various Russian regions, it does not have a direct connection to [[ukraine|Ukraine]], yet its mention is relevant in the context of regional geography and historical ties between Ukraine and Russia.

title: Pecherskyi District
summary: Pecherskyi District is an urban district in Kyiv, the capital of Ukraine, encompassing the historical Pechersk neighborhood and several other notable areas. It serves as a significant cultural, political, and administrative center within the city.

title: pensions in Ukraine
summary: Pensions in Ukraine serve as a financial support system for retirees, structured under a three-tiered system established by the [[law-of-ukraine|Law of Ukraine]] on Compulsory State Pension Insurance. This system is crucial for addressing the needs of the aging population and ensuring financial stability for retirees in the country.

title: Pereiaslav
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Pereiaslav is a historical city located in Boryspil Raion, [[kyiv-oblast|Kyiv Oblast]], central [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. Known for its rich history and cultural significance, it serves as the administrative center of the Pereiaslav urban hromada and hosts a population of approximately 26,273 as of 2022.

title: Peremyshl
summary: Peremyshl refers to multiple locations, including a village in Russia and a historical town in Muscovy, with relevance to the broader context of Eastern European geography.

title: Pervomaisk
summary: Pervomaisk is a term commonly used in the former Soviet Union, originating from the May Day holiday, known as International Workers' Day. In the context of Ukraine, it refers to several locations within the country.

title: Petro Poroshenko
summary: Petro Oleksiiovych Poroshenko is a prominent Ukrainian politician and businessman who served as the fifth president of Ukraine from 2014 to 2019. His leadership was marked by significant military and economic reforms, as well as a strong push for Ukraine's integration with the European Union.

title: Petrykivka painting
summary: Petrykivka painting is a traditional Ukrainian decorative art form that originated in the village of Petrykivka, [[dnipropetrovsk-oblast|Dnipropetrovsk Oblast]]. Recognized for its vibrant floral patterns and unique brush techniques, this style has been an integral part of Ukrainian culture since the 18th century and continues to evolve as a modern art form.

title: Pidhirtsi Castle
summary: Pidhirtsi Castle, located in the village of Pidhirtsi in [[lviv-oblast|Lviv Oblast]], [[ukraine|Ukraine]], is a historically significant residential castle-fortress built between 1635 and 1640. It is recognized as a valuable example of the palace-garden complexes from the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth era.

title: Pivdenmash
summary: Pivdenmash, officially known as the State Enterprise 'Production Amalgamation Southern Machine-Building Plant named after O.M. Makarov', is a state-owned aerospace and defense manufacturer [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], located in Dnipro. Established as a Soviet factory, Pivdenmash has played a significant role in missile production and space exploration, contributing to [[ukraine|Ukraine]]'s industrial and technological landscape.

title: Pochayiv Lavra
summary: The Holy Dormition Pochaiv Lavra, also referred to as the Pochaiv Monastery, is a significant Orthodox monastery located in Pochaiv, Kremenets Raion, [[ternopil-oblast|Ternopil Oblast]], Ukraine. It has served as a key spiritual center for Eastern Orthodoxy and Greek Catholicism throughout its history, with recent developments solidifying its status within the Orthodox Church of Ukraine.

title: Podil
summary: Podil, also referred to as Podol, is a historic district in Kyiv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], known as the Lower City. It is one of the oldest neighborhoods in the city, serving as a center for trade, commerce, and industry since its establishment.

title: Podolia
summary: Podolia, also known as Podillia, is a historic region in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]], primarily situated in the west-central and southwestern parts of [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. It has a rich agricultural landscape and a complex history involving various empires and nations, significantly influencing Ukrainian culture and identity.

title: Pohrebyshche
summary: Pohrebyshche is a small city located in Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine, historically significant as the administrative center of Pohrebyshche Raion until its dissolution in 2020. The city, with a population of 9,209 as of 2022, is situated near the Ros River and has a rich historical background dating back to its first mention in 1148.

title: Polesia
summary: Polesia, also known as Palessie, Polissia, or Polesie, is a significant natural and historical region in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]], prominently featuring the Belarus–Ukraine border and parts of eastern Poland. It is recognized for its extensive forested areas and marshlands, particularly relevant to Ukraine's geography and history.

title: political party in Ukraine
summary: Political parties in Ukraine play a crucial role in the country's multi-party system, which has evolved significantly since independence in 1991. The landscape is characterized by a variety of parties, often influenced by oligarchs, and a low level of public trust in these political entities.

title: Poltava
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Poltava is a city located on the [[vorskla|Vorskla River]] in Central Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Poltava Oblast and Poltava Raion. With an estimated population of 279,593 in 2022, it holds significant historical and cultural relevance in Ukraine.

title: Poltava Oblast
summary: Poltava Oblast, known as Poltavshchyna, is a province located in central Ukraine, with its administrative center in the city of Poltava. The oblast, which has a population of approximately 1,352,283 as of 2022, is historically significant as part of the Cossack Hetmanate and plays a crucial role [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s cultural and economic landscape.

title: polygon
summary: A polygon is a two-dimensional geometric figure composed of line segments that form a closed shape. Polygons are significant in various fields, including mathematics, architecture, and art, and have relevance in Ukraine's cultural and educational contexts.

title: Post-Soviet states
summary: The post-Soviet states, consisting of 15 independent nations that emerged following the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991, play a significant role in the geopolitical landscape of Ukraine and its neighboring regions. This cultural region includes countries that were once Union Republics and highlights the complex historical and political ties among them.

title: Postbank
summary: Postbank refers to various banking institutions and systems associated with postal services across different countries. This entry highlights the relevance of these institutions, including their potential connections to Ukraine and the broader context of postal banking services.

title: potato pancake
summary: Potato pancakes, known in Ukraine as деруни (deruny), are shallow-fried pancakes made primarily from grated potatoes, often combined with ingredients like flour and eggs. This dish is a staple in [[ukrainian-cuisine|Ukrainian cuisine]] and is celebrated for its simplicity and flavor.

title: Pravda
summary: Pravda is a historically significant Russian newspaper that served as the official publication of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union. Its connection to Ukraine is evident through its early editorial influences and the involvement of various factions, including Ukrainian political groups, during its formative years.

title: President of Ukraine
summary: The President of Ukraine serves as the head of state, representing the nation in international affairs and overseeing the executive branch of government. Elected by the citizens for a five-year term, the office has been pivotal in shaping Ukraine's political landscape since its establishment in 1991.

title: Prime Minister of Ukraine
summary: The Prime Minister of Ukraine serves as the head of government, overseeing the Cabinet of Ministers, the highest executive body in the country. This position has evolved since Ukraine's independence in 1991, with various notable individuals holding the office, including the first female prime minister, Yulia Tymoshenko.

title: Pripyat
summary: Pripyat, an abandoned industrial city in [[kyiv-oblast|Kyiv Oblast]], [[ukraine|Ukraine]], was founded on 4 February 1970 and is closely associated with the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant. The city was evacuated following the Chernobyl disaster on 27 April 1986, leading to its abandonment and subsequent historical significance.

title: Pripyat River
summary: The Pripyat River, also known as Prypiat, is a significant waterway in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]], measuring approximately 761 km (473 mi) in length. It flows predominantly through Ukraine and Belarus, ultimately draining into the Dnieper at the Kyiv Reservoir, highlighting its relevance to the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] landscape and history.

title: PrivatBank
summary: PrivatBank is the largest bank in Ukraine by assets, established on 19 March 1992. It has been state-owned since its nationalization in 2016 and is recognized as one of the country's systemically important banks.

title: Prizrak
summary: Prizrak (Ghost) is a 2015 Russian comedy film directed by Aleksandr Voytinskiy, featuring actors Fedor Bondarchuk and Semyon Treskunov. The film is notable for being the first Russian production to utilize Dolby Atmos technology and has garnered approximately 383 million Russian rubles at the box office.

title: Prosvita
summary: Prosvita, officially known as the All-Ukrainian Prosvita Society named after [[taras-shevchenko|Taras Shevchenko]], is an enlightenment organization established in the 19th century to promote and preserve Ukrainian culture, education, and science. It has played a significant role in counteracting Russophile influences within Ukrainian society.

title: Protestantism in Ukraine
summary: Protestantism in Ukraine encompasses a diverse range of denominations and has a significant presence, with approximately 1.7 million adherents, representing about 3.8% of the population as of 2010. The movement has deep historical roots in the region, dating back to the 16th century, and has evolved into a vital part of the country's religious landscape.

title: Prut
summary: The Prut River, a significant left tributary of the Danube, spans 953 km (592 mi) and plays a crucial role in the geography and history of [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]], particularly in relation to Ukraine. Originating in the Carpathian Mountains of Ukraine, the river forms part of the border between Ukraine and Romania.

title: Prykarpattia
summary: Prykarpattia, also referred to as Subcarpathia, is a geographical region [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] located at the northeastern foothills of the [[carpathians|Carpathian Mountains]]. It primarily encompasses Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast and parts of Lviv Oblast, forming a significant part of the historic region of [[galicia|Galicia]].

title: Psycho-Pass
summary: Psycho-Pass is a Japanese cyberpunk psychological thriller anime series that aired from October 2012 to March 2013, produced by Production I.G. The series explores themes of governance and morality within a dystopian society, and its relevance extends to Ukraine through discussions of surveillance and authoritarianism.

title: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky
summary: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky was a prominent Russian composer of the Romantic era, born on 7 May 1840 and passing away on 6 November 1893. His works, which include notable pieces such as the 1812 Overture and the ballets Swan Lake and The Nutcracker, have had a lasting impact on classical music and are significant within the cultural context of Ukraine.

title: Pyriatyn
summary: Pyriatyn is a city located in Poltava Oblast, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], recognized as an important industrial hub in the region. As of 2022, the estimated population of the city is 14,988.

title: Pyrohiv
summary: Pyrohiv is a former village that has evolved into a residential neighborhood located on the southern outskirts of Kyiv, within the Holosiivskyi District. It is notable for its historical significance and cultural institutions, including the National Museum of Folk Architecture and Folkways of Ukraine.

title: pysanka
summary: Pysanka is a traditional Ukrainian practice of egg decoration, particularly associated with Easter, that has roots in both pagan and Christian customs. This art form, characterized by intricate designs created using a wax-resist technique, is recognized as a national symbol of Ukraine and has influenced various cultural practices both domestically and internationally.

title: Pysanka Museum
summary: The Pysanka Museum, located in Kolomyia, [[ivano-frankivsk-oblast|Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast]], Ukraine, is the world's only museum dedicated to the art of pysanka, or Ukrainian Easter eggs. Opened on October 26, 1987, it serves as a significant cultural institution showcasing the rich tradition of pysanka [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

title: Radio Ukraine
summary: Radio Ukraine is a publicly funded radio broadcaster in Ukraine, established in 1924. It operates under the National Public Broadcasting Company of Ukraine and serves as a significant platform for news, culture, and music across the country.

title: Radomysl Castle
summary: Radomysl Castle, located in Radomyshl, [[zhytomyr-oblast|Zhytomyr Oblast]], [[ukraine|Ukraine]], is a historical and cultural complex established between 2007 and 2011 by Ukrainian doctor and public activist Olha Bohomolets. The site features a museum dedicated to Ukrainian home icons and is part of the Council of Europe's cultural project, Via Regia.

title: rag doll
summary: A rag doll is a type of doll crafted from fabric scraps, historically serving as both a toy and a tool for teaching sewing skills. In Ukraine, the motanka doll represents a traditional variant of the rag doll, deeply rooted in folk culture and magical beliefs.

title: rail transport in Ukraine
type: rail transport by country or region
summary: Rail transport in Ukraine serves as a critical mode of transportation for both passengers and freight, predominantly managed by the state-owned Ukrzaliznytsia. The railway network, largely established during the Russian Empire and the Soviet Union, has faced significant challenges due to ongoing conflicts and modernization efforts.

title: Ramstein Air Base
summary: Ramstein Air Base is a significant United States Air Force installation located in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, serving as the headquarters for the U.S. Air Forces in Europe and NATO Allied Air Command. The base plays a crucial role in military operations, particularly in relation to Eastern Europe, including Ukraine.

title: Rava-Ruska
summary: Rava-Ruska is a city located in Lviv Raion, Lviv Oblast, in western Ukraine, serving as a border town adjacent to Poland. The city has a population of approximately 8,494 as of 2022 and plays a significant role in the administrative structure of Ukraine as the center of the Rava-Ruska urban hromada.

title: religion in Ukraine
summary: Religion in Ukraine is predominantly Christian, with 85% of the population identifying as Christian as of 2022. The landscape of religious affiliation is marked by a significant presence of Eastern Orthodoxy and Catholicism, alongside smaller religious communities.

title: Renaissance Capital
summary: Renaissance Capital is an investment bank established in 1995, primarily focused on Russian and frontier markets, with significant operations [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] and other emerging economies. The firm, which became part of ONEXIM Group in 2012, offers a wide range of investment banking services and has a notable presence in Africa.

title: Republic of Abkhazia
summary: The Republic of Abkhazia is a partially recognized state located in the South Caucasus, which is predominantly regarded as part of Georgia by the international community. Its complex history, marked by ethnic tensions and conflict, has significant implications for regional stability, including its relations with [[ukraine|Ukraine]].

title: Republic of Ukraine
summary: The Republic of Ukraine emerged following its independence from the Soviet Union in 1991, marking a significant transition in its governance and constitution. This entry outlines the geographical, historical, and political context of Ukraine during the post-Soviet era.

title: Revolution of Dignity
summary: The Revolution of Dignity, also known as the Maidan Revolution, occurred [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] in February 2014 as a culmination of the Euromaidan protests. This civil disorder led to the ousting of President Viktor Yanukovych and significant political changes in Ukraine, ultimately contributing to the Russo-Ukrainian war.

title: Rivne
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Rivne is a city of regional significance in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of Rivne Oblast and [[rivne-raion|Rivne Raion]]. With a population of 243,873 as of 2022, it has a rich historical background and plays a crucial role in the region's transportation and industry.

title: Rivne Nuclear Power Plant
summary: Rivne Nuclear Power Plant, located in Rivne Oblast, Ukraine, is notable for being the first site in the country to operate VVER-440 reactors. The facility plays a significant role in Ukraine's energy sector, contributing a substantial portion of the country's nuclear electricity generation.

title: Rivne Oblast
summary: Rivne Oblast, known in Ukrainian as Рівненська область, is an administrative region in northwestern Ukraine with its center in the city of Rivne. Covering an area of 20,100 square kilometers, it had an estimated population of 1,141,784 in 2022.

title: Rivne Raion
summary: Rivne Raion is an administrative district located in Rivne Oblast, western Ukraine, with its administrative center in the city of Rivne. As of 2022, the population of the raion is estimated to be 625,543.

title: Rohatyn
summary: Rohatyn is a city situated on the Hnyla Lypa River in Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast, western Ukraine, with a population of 7,521 as of 2022. It serves as the administrative center of the Rohatyn urban hromada and has a rich historical and cultural significance, particularly in relation to its Jewish community and notable historical figures.

title: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Lviv
summary: The Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Lviv is a significant ecclesiastical jurisdiction of the Latin Church located in western Ukraine. It serves as a metropolitan archdiocese with historical roots dating back to the 14th century and plays a vital role in the Catholic community of Ukraine.

title: Roman Sushchenko
summary: Roman Volodymyrovych Sushchenko is a Ukrainian journalist and artist, notable for his arrest in Russia on espionage charges in 2016 and subsequent detention until his release in 2019. His case has drawn significant attention and criticism from various Ukrainian and international organizations.

title: Romania–Ukraine relations
summary: Romania–Ukraine relations encompass the diplomatic and bilateral interactions between Romania and Ukraine, which were first established on February 9, 1918, and re-established in 1992. The relationship has been shaped by historical disputes and ongoing cooperation, particularly in the context of regional security and minority rights.

title: Rosava River
summary: The Rosava is a river situated [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], recognized as a left-bank tributary of the Ros River. It spans 90 kilometers and serves a basin area of 1,720 square kilometers.

title: Roshen
summary: Roshen Confectionery Corporation is a prominent Ukrainian confectionery manufacturing group, known for its extensive production and export of various confectionery products. Founded in 1993, the company has become a significant player in the global candy industry, with its operations deeply rooted in Ukraine.

title: Rus
summary: The term 'Rus' or 'RUS' encompasses a variety of historical, cultural, and geographical references, particularly significant in the context of East Slavic history and its connection to Ukraine.

title: Rus' Khaganate
summary: The Rus' Khaganate, a term used by historians, refers to a proposed political entity believed to have existed in Eastern Europe from approximately 830 to the 890s. Its connection to the early formation of Kievan Rus', a significant historical state [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], remains a topic of scholarly debate.

title: Rus' people
summary: The Rus', also referred to as Russes, were an early medieval ethnic group in Eastern Europe, primarily of Norse origin, who played a significant role in the formation of Kievan Rus' and the cultural development of Ukraine and its neighboring regions.

title: Rusal
summary: United Company Rusal is the world's second-largest aluminium producer, with significant operations and historical ties to [[ukraine|Ukraine]], particularly through its ownership of the Nikolaev alumina refinery. Founded by Oleg Deripaska, Rusal has undergone various mergers and expansions since its inception in 2000.

title: Rusalka
summary: In Slavic folklore, the rusalka, a female entity often associated with water, has significant ties to [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] culture. Known for its dual nature, the rusalka can embody both benevolence and malevolence, reflecting a complex relationship with humanity and nature.

title: Rushnyk
summary: A rushnyk is a decorative and ritual cloth significant in Ukrainian culture, often made of linen or cotton and featuring intricate woven or embroidered designs. It plays a vital role in various East Slavic rituals, including weddings and funerals, and serves as a symbol of cultural heritage.

title: Ruslana Lyzhychko
summary: Ruslana Stepanivna Lyzhychko, born on 24 May 1973 in Lviv, Ukraine, is a prominent Ukrainian singer, songwriter, producer, activist, and former politician. She gained international fame after winning the Eurovision Song Contest in 2004 and is recognized as one of the most successful Ukrainian female artists globally.

title: Russian annexation of Crimea
summary: The Russian annexation of Crimea occurred in 2014, following an invasion of the peninsula, which is part of Ukraine. This event marked a significant escalation in the ongoing [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|Russo-Ukrainian war]] and has been widely condemned by Ukraine and the international community as a violation of international law.

title: Russian occupation of Crimea
summary: The Russian occupation of Crimea, which began in 2014, has significant implications for Ukraine's territorial integrity and international relations. Following the military intervention by Russia, Crimea was annexed, a move that remains unrecognized by Ukraine and the majority of the global community.

title: Russian Revolution of 1905
summary: The Russian Revolution of 1905, also referred to as the First Russian Revolution, was a significant uprising within the Russian Empire that commenced on 22 January 1905, ultimately resulting in the establishment of a constitutional monarchy through the Russian Constitution of 1906. This revolution was marked by widespread political and social unrest, including strikes and revolts that had implications for Ukraine's socio-political landscape.

title: Russian war crimes
summary: Russian war crimes encompass violations of international criminal law, including war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide, attributed to Russian armed forces and associated paramilitary groups since the dissolution of [[soviet-union|the Soviet Union]] in 1991. These crimes have been particularly relevant in the context of Ukraine, where significant allegations have emerged during the ongoing conflict.
aliases: war crimes of the Russian Federation

title: Russia–Ukraine relations
summary: Russia-Ukraine relations have been characterized by conflict and tension, particularly following Russia's annexation of Crimea in 2014 and the subsequent outbreak of [[war-in-donbas|war in eastern Ukraine]]. Diplomatic relations have ceased entirely since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

title: Russo-Ukrainian war
summary: The Russo-Ukrainian war, which commenced in February 2014, has significantly impacted Ukraine following the occupation and [[russian-annexation-of-crimea|annexation of Crimea by Russia]]. The conflict has evolved through various phases, including support for separatist movements in eastern Ukraine and a full-scale invasion by Russia in February 2022, marking the largest military conflict in Europe since World War II.
aliases: Special operation on the territory of Ukraine

title: Rusyns
summary: Rusyns, also referred to as Carpatho-Rusyns or Ruthenians, are an East Slavic ethnic group primarily located in the Eastern Carpathians, with a significant presence in Ukraine. They speak the Rusyn language, which is debated as either a separate language or a dialect of Ukrainian, and have a unique cultural identity recognized in several Central and Eastern European countries.

title: Ruthenia
summary: Ruthenia is a historical region associated with the East Slavic peoples, particularly Ukrainians and Belarusians, encompassing parts of modern Belarus, Ukraine, Eastern Poland, and western Russia. The term has evolved over centuries, reflecting the complex historical and cultural ties of these territories to Ukraine.

title: Ruthenian
summary: Ruthenian was a written language utilized from the 14th to the 18th centuries in the East Slavic-speaking regions of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. It is recognized as a historical precursor to modern Belarusian and Ukrainian languages.
aliases: Chancery language of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania

title: Saint George's Cathedral
summary: Saint George's Cathedral, known in Ukrainian as Собор святого Юра, is a baroque-rococo cathedral situated in Lviv, a significant city in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]]. Constructed between 1744 and 1760, it has played a crucial role in the religious and cultural landscape of Ukraine, particularly as the mother church of the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church during the 19th and 20th centuries.

title: Saint Sophia Cathedral
summary: Saint Sophia Cathedral, located in Kyiv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], is a significant architectural monument from the era of [[kievan-rus|Kyivan Rus]]'. It is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site and serves as a museum and a key component of the National Reserve 'Sophia of Kyiv'.

title: Sakhalin
summary: Sakhalin is the largest island of Russia, located in Northeast Asia, with a complex history of territorial claims involving China, Russia, and Japan. Its geographical significance and historical connections to indigenous peoples, including the Ainu, Oroks, and Nivkhs, highlight its relevance to regional dynamics, including its ties to [[ukraine|Ukraine]] through historical trade and migration patterns.

title: Sakharov Prize
summary: The Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought is an honorary award recognizing individuals and groups committed to human rights and freedom of thought. Established by the European Parliament in December 1988 and named after Andrei Sakharov, the prize has significant relevance to Ukraine's human rights landscape.
aliases: Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought

title: salo
summary: Salo, also known as slanina, is a traditional European food made from salt-cured pork fat, particularly significant in [[ukrainian-cuisine|Ukrainian cuisine]]. It is characterized by its preparation methods and cultural importance across Central, Eastern, and Southeastern Europe.

title: Sambir
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Sambir is a city of regional significance located in Lviv Oblast, Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Sambir Raion. With a population of approximately 34,152 in 2022, it is notable for its historical significance and strategic location near the Polish border.

title: Samopomich
summary: The Association 'Self Reliance' (Ukrainian: Об'єднання «Самопоміч») is a [[political-party-in-ukraine|political party in Ukraine]] that embodies liberal conservative and Christian democratic ideologies. Founded on 29 December 2012, it has its roots in the Ukrainian cooperative movement and has participated in various elections, achieving notable successes and challenges.

title: Sarmatians
summary: The Sarmatians were a significant confederation of ancient Iranian nomadic peoples who inhabited the Pontic steppe from approximately the 5th century BC to the 4th century AD. Their history is deeply intertwined with the region that includes modern-day Ukraine, where they played a crucial role in the cultural and political landscape of the time.

title: Sarny
summary: Sarny is a small city located in [[rivne-oblast|Rivne Oblast]], [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of Sarny Raion. With a population of 28,626 as of 2022, it is a significant railway hub situated on the Sluch River.

title: Savchuk
summary: Savchuk is a Ukrainian surname that is prevalent in several countries, including Poland, Israel, Russia, and the United States. The name is associated with various notable individuals, particularly in the fields of sports and the arts, many of whom have Ukrainian heritage.

title: Scythians
summary: The Scythians, also referred to as the Pontic Scythians, were an ancient nomadic people of Eastern Iranic origin who migrated to the Pontic Steppe in modern-day Ukraine and Southern Russia from Central Asia during the 9th to 8th centuries BC. They played a significant role in the history of the Eurasian Steppe until their eventual decline by the 3rd century AD.

title: Second Battle of Kharkov
summary: The Second Battle of Kharkov, also known as Operation Fredericus, was an Axis counter-offensive that took place from May 12 to May 28, 1942, in the Kharkov region of [[ukraine|Ukraine]] during World War II. This battle aimed to eliminate the Soviet Izium bridgehead and resulted in a significant German victory, impacting the course of the war on the Eastern Front.

title: Security Service of Ukraine
summary: The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) is the primary internal security agency of Ukraine, tasked with counter-intelligence, organized crime, and terrorism prevention. Established in 1991 following Ukraine's independence, the SBU has undergone significant changes in its structure and operations, particularly after the Revolution of Dignity in 2014.

title: Sergei Bubka
summary: Serhiy Nazarovych Bubka is a distinguished Ukrainian former pole vaulter, recognized as the 1988 Olympic Champion and a record six-time consecutive World Champion. His remarkable achievements in athletics and contributions to sports governance have made him a significant figure [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s sporting history.

title: Sergei Korolev
summary: Sergei Pavlovich Korolev was a prominent Soviet rocket engineer and spacecraft designer, instrumental in the early Soviet space program and a key figure in the Space Race. His connections to Ukraine are significant, as he was born in Zhytomyr and spent formative years in the region.

title: Serhiy Haidai
summary: Serhiy Volodymyrovych Haidai is a Ukrainian entrepreneur and politician who served as the head of the Luhansk Regional Military–Civil Administration during a critical period of the Russian [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|invasion of Ukraine]]. His career includes significant administrative roles in various [[administrative-territorial-entity-of-ukraine|regions of Ukraine]], particularly in Luhansk and [[transcarpathia|Zakarpattia]] Oblasts.

title: Serhiy Zhadan
summary: Serhiy Viktorovych Zhadan is a prominent Ukrainian poet, novelist, musician, translator, and social activist, born on 23 August 1974 in Starobilsk, Luhansk Oblast, Ukraine. He is known for his contributions to contemporary [[ukrainian-literature|Ukrainian literature]] and his active role in political and social movements within the country.

title: Servant of the People
summary: Servant of the People is a liberal, centrist [[political-party-in-ukraine|political party in Ukraine]], known for its association with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Since the 2019 elections, it has held a ruling position in the [[cabinet-of-ministers-of-ukraine|Ukrainian government]].

title: Sevastopol
summary: Sevastopol is the largest city in [[crimean-khanate|Crimea]] and a significant port on the Black Sea, founded in 1783 by Catherine the Great. The city has a complex history marked by its strategic military importance and its contentious status following the annexation of Crimea by Russia in 2014, despite being internationally recognized as part of Ukraine.

title: Shatsk National Natural Park
summary: Shatsk National Natural Park is a significant national park in Ukraine, established in 1983 to conserve the unique natural environments of Volyn Polissia. Covering an area of 490 square kilometers, it is home to the Svitiaz Lake, the deepest lake in Ukraine, and a diverse range of flora and fauna, making it an important ecological and recreational area.

title: Shche ne vmerla Ukrainy i slava, i volia
summary: The State Anthem of Ukraine, known by its incipit 'Shche ne vmerla Ukrainy i slava, i volia', is a significant symbol of Ukrainian national identity and pride. The anthem's lyrics, composed by Pavlo Chubynskyi in 1862, were set to music by Mykhailo Verbytskyi in 1863, and it was officially adopted as the national anthem in 1992.
aliases: Shche ne vmerla Ukrainy ni slava, ni volia

title: Shchedryk
summary: Shchedryk is a term associated with various cultural and artistic elements rooted in Ukrainian heritage, including a traditional song and a children's choir. It also refers to a film that highlights Ukrainian history.

title: Sheptytskyi
summary: Sheptytskyi is a historical mining town located in [[lviv-oblast|Lviv Oblast]], [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of Sheptytskyi Raion. The town, formerly known as Chervonohrad and Krystynopol, has a rich history and a diverse population, with significant connections to the Jewish community and coal mining industry.

title: Shevchenko National Prize
summary: The Shevchenko National Prize is the highest state award [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] for achievements in culture and arts, established in 1961 and named after the influential Ukrainian poet Taras Shevchenko. It recognizes outstanding contributions across various artistic fields, reflecting the nation's cultural heritage.

title: shipbuilding in Ukraine
summary: Shipbuilding in Ukraine has a long history, beginning during the Cossack era and evolving through various historical periods, including the Soviet period and into independence. The industry is significant for its contributions to both military and civilian maritime capabilities.

title: Siberia
summary: Siberia is a vast geographical region that encompasses all of North Asia, extending from the Ural Mountains to the Pacific Ocean. It has been part of Russia since the late 16th century and holds historical significance, including its cultural connections to various ethnic groups, some of which are relevant to Ukraine's historical narratives.

title: Sich Riflemen
summary: The Sich Riflemen Halych-Bukovyna Kurin was a significant military unit of the [[ukrainians|Ukrainian People]]'s Army, active from 1917 to 1919. Composed of Ukrainian soldiers from the Austro-Hungarian army and local volunteers, the unit played a crucial role [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s struggle for independence during the tumultuous period following World War I.

title: Siege of Chernihiv
summary: The Siege of Chernihiv was a significant military conflict that took place in the city of Chernihiv, located in [[chernihiv-oblast|Chernihiv Oblast]], Ukraine, during the [[2022-russian-invasion-of-ukraine|2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]. The siege began on 24 February 2022 and lasted until early April 2022, resulting in extensive destruction and civilian casualties.

title: Siege of Mariupol
summary: The Siege of Mariupol, which commenced on 24 February 2022 and concluded on 20 May 2022, was a critical military engagement during the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The siege resulted in significant casualties and destruction, marking a pivotal moment in the conflict over control of southeastern Ukraine.

title: Siverskodonetsk
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Siverskodonetsk, previously known as Sievierodonetsk, is a city of regional significance located in Luhansk Oblast, eastern Ukraine. It has a rich industrial history and has been significantly impacted by the ongoing conflict in the region.

title: Slavic religion
summary: Slavic religion refers to the pre-Christian spiritual beliefs, mythologies, and rituals of the Slavic peoples, which were practiced until their gradual Christianization from the 8th to the 13th centuries. This polytheistic and animistic faith, with deep ties to nature and agricultural cycles, played a significant role in the cultural [[history-of-ukraine|history of Ukraine]] and the broader Slavic world.

title: Slavutych
summary: Slavutych is a city in northern [[ukraine|Ukraine]], established in 1986 to accommodate personnel evacuated from the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant following the nuclear disaster. It is located in [[chernihiv-oblast|Chernihiv Oblast]] and serves as an administrative exclave of Kyiv Oblast.

title: Snake Island
summary: Snake Island, also referred to as Serpent Island, is a Ukrainian island in the Black Sea that plays a significant role in defining Ukraine's territorial waters. Historically significant and strategically important, the island has been involved in various geopolitical disputes and conflicts, particularly between Ukraine and Romania.

title: Snake Island campaign
summary: The Snake Island campaign refers to the Russian military's attack and subsequent occupation of Snake Island, a strategically significant Ukrainian island in the Black Sea, beginning on 24 February 2022, the first day of the Russian [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|invasion of Ukraine]]. The campaign lasted for 126 days and involved notable Ukrainian resistance and counteroffensive actions.

title: Social Democratic Party of Ukraine (united)
summary: The Social Democratic Party of Ukraine (united), abbreviated SDPU(o), is a [[political-party-in-ukraine|political party in Ukraine]] that emerged from earlier social democratic factions. Initially influential in the 1990s, the party has faced significant decline since the early 2000s, particularly following the Orange Revolution.

title: Sofia Rotaru
summary: Sofiia Mykhailivna Yevdokymenko-Rotaru, commonly known as Sofia Rotaru, is a prominent [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] singer born on 7 August 1947. She has made significant contributions to the music scene in Ukraine and the [[post-soviet-states|former Soviet Union]], achieving international recognition through her diverse repertoire and performances.

title: Sofiyivsky Park
summary: Sofiyivsky Park, located in Uman, Cherkasy Oblast, Ukraine, is an arboretum and scientific-research institute affiliated with the [[national-academy-of-sciences-of-ukraine|National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]]. Established in 1796 by Count Stanisław Szczęsny Potocki, the park features over 2,000 species of trees and is recognized as a significant example of early 19th-century landscape gardening.

title: Soledar
summary: Soledar is a city in Bakhmut Raion, [[donetsk-oblast|Donetsk Oblast]], Ukraine, known for its historical salt mining industry. Once a thriving settlement, it has been largely destroyed and depopulated due to the ongoing conflict in the region, particularly during the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

title: Southern Bug
summary: The Southern Bug, also known as Southern Buh, is a navigable river located entirely within Ukraine, recognized as the second-longest river in the country. It plays a significant role in the geography, history, and [[economy-of-ukraine|economy of Ukraine]].

title: Soviet famine of 1932–1933
summary: The Soviet famine of 1932–1933 was a catastrophic event that primarily affected Ukraine and other grain-producing regions of the Soviet Union, resulting in millions of deaths due to starvation. The famine was largely driven by policies of forced collectivization and grain procurement mandated by the Soviet government under Joseph Stalin.

title: Soviet invasion of Poland
summary: The Soviet invasion of Poland was a military operation conducted by the Soviet Union on 17 September 1939, occurring shortly after the Nazi invasion from the west. This invasion resulted in the division and annexation of Poland between the Soviet Union and Nazi Germany, significantly impacting [[ukraine|Ukraine]]'s borders and demographics.

title: Soviet occupation of Ukraine
summary: The Soviet occupation of Ukraine encompasses various military actions and territorial changes involving Soviet forces from the early 20th century to the mid-20th century, significantly impacting the region's history and its relationship with the Soviet Union.

title: Soviet Union
summary: The Soviet Union, officially known as the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR), was a significant transcontinental entity from 1922 until its dissolution in 1991, encompassing a vast area of Eurasia, including Ukraine. As a federal union of national republics, the Soviet Union was characterized by its centralized governance and communist ideology, playing a crucial role in global events, particularly during World War II and the Cold War.
aliases: the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics

title: State Emergency Service of Ukraine
summary: The State Emergency Service of Ukraine is the primary executive body responsible for implementing state policies related to civil defense, emergency response, and disaster management [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]. Established in 1996, it plays a crucial role in protecting the population and territory from emergencies, including the aftermath of the Chernobyl disaster.

title: State Property Fund of Ukraine
summary: The State Property Fund of Ukraine is a central executive body that oversees the management and privatization of state property in Ukraine, operating under the administration of the Cabinet of Ministers.

title: State Statistics Service of Ukraine
summary: The State Statistics Service of Ukraine is the governmental agency tasked with the collection and dissemination of statistical data in Ukraine. Established in 2010, it plays a crucial role in aligning Ukrainian statistics with international standards and supporting the country's European integration efforts.

title: State University of Trade and Economics
summary: The State University of Trade and Economics (SUTE) is a prominent [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] institution located in Kyiv, specializing in trade and economics education. Established from the Kyiv branch of the All-Union Correspondence Institute of Soviet Trade in 1946, the university has undergone several transformations and name changes, reflecting its evolving role in Ukraine's higher education landscape.
