title: Stepan Bandera
summary: Stepan Andriiovych Bandera (1 January 1909 – 15 October 1959) was a prominent Ukrainian far-right leader associated with the radical faction of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists, known as OUN-B. His actions and ideology have made him a controversial figure [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s history, particularly regarding his role in the nationalist movement and World War II.

title: Sudak
summary: Sudak is a city located in Crimea, recognized by most countries as part of [[ukraine|Ukraine]] but annexed by Russia. It serves as the administrative center of Sudak Municipality and is known for its historical significance and tourist attractions, particularly the Genoese fortress.

title: Sumy
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Sumy is a city of regional significance located in northeastern Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of [[sumy-oblast|Sumy Oblast]]. Founded in the 1650s by [[cossacks|Cossacks]], Sumy has evolved into a significant industrial and cultural hub in Northern Ukraine, with a population of 256,474 as of 2022.

title: Sumy Oblast
summary: Sumy Oblast is a province located in northeastern Ukraine, established in 1939 through the amalgamation of territories from neighboring oblasts. It serves as a significant cultural and economic region within Ukraine, with a diverse demographic and historical background.

title: Sviatohirsk
summary: Sviatohirsk is a city located in the northern part of [[donetsk-oblast|Donetsk Oblast]], Ukraine, situated along the Siverskyi Donets River. With a population of 4,226 as of 2022, the city is notable for its historical significance, particularly the 16th-century Sviatohirsk Lavra Monastery.

title: Sviatohirsk Lavra
summary: Sviatohirsk Lavra, officially known as the Holy Mountains Lavra of the Holy Dormition, is a significant Orthodox Christian monastery located in eastern Ukraine, near the town of Sviatohirsk in [[donetsk-oblast|Donetsk Oblast]]. Established in the 15th century, it has a rich history marked by periods of closure, restoration, and recent conflict.

title: Sviatoshyn
summary: Sviatoshyn is a historic neighborhood and suburb of Kyiv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], located on the western edge of the city. Originally a dacha village, it has evolved into a significant residential area with historical and cultural relevance.

title: Sviatoshynskyi District
summary: Sviatoshynskyi District is an urban district located in the western part of Kyiv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. Established in 2001, it was formerly known as Leningrad District and is named after the historical neighborhood of Sviatoshyn, which honors the 12th-century Prince Mykola Sviatosha.

title: Sviatoslav I of Kiev
summary: Sviatoslav I of Kiev (c. 943 – 972) was a significant ruler of the Kievan Rus', known for his military campaigns that led to the decline of Khazaria and the First Bulgarian Empire. His reign marked a period of territorial expansion and the establishment of Kievan Rus' as a major power in Eastern Europe.

title: Sviatoslav Vakarchuk
summary: Sviatoslav Ivanovych '[[moskva|Slava]]' Vakarchuk is a prominent [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] musician, politician, public activist, and soldier, best known as the lead vocalist of the rock band Okean Elzy. He has played a significant role in Ukraine's cultural and political landscape, notably during key historical events such as the [[orange-revolution|Orange Revolution]] and Euromaidan.

title: Svitlovodsk
summary: Svitlovodsk is a city situated on the Dnieper River in Oleksandriia Raion, Kirovohrad Oblast, [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. It serves as the administrative center of the Svitlovodsk urban hromada and has an estimated population of approximately 43,130 as of 2022.

title: Syvash Bay
summary: Syvash Bay, also known as the Putrid Sea or Rotten Sea, is a significant area of shallow lagoons located on the western edge of the Sea of Azov, closely associated with [[ukraine|Ukraine]]'s geographical and ecological landscape. It covers approximately 2,560 km2 and is recognized as a wetland of international importance under the Ramsar Convention.

title: Taras Bulba
summary: Taras Bulba is a romanticized historical novella by [[nikolai-gogol|Nikolai Gogol]], set in the first half of the 17th century, that centers around the Zaporozhian Cossack Taras Bulba and his sons. The work is significant in Ukrainian literature, highlighting themes of patriotism and the struggle against Polish rule in Ukraine.

title: Taras Shevchenko
summary: Taras Hryhorovych Shevchenko (9 March 1814 – 10 March 1861) was a prominent Ukrainian poet, writer, artist, and political figure, whose works are foundational to modern Ukrainian literature and language. His literary and artistic contributions have made him a significant cultural icon in Ukraine and among Slavic nations.

title: Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv
summary: The Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv is a prominent public university located in Kyiv, Ukraine, recognized as the third-oldest university in the country. Established in 1834, it has evolved into a leading center for education and research, named after the influential Ukrainian poet and artist Taras Shevchenko.
aliases: Kyiv National University named after Taras Shevchenko

title: Tawrija
summary: Tavria is a geographic term referring to a subregion in Southern Ukraine, notable for its steppe landscape situated between the Dnipro and Molochna rivers and the Crimean peninsula. The term also encompasses historical administrative divisions and contemporary institutions relevant to Ukraine.

title: telecommunications in Ukraine
summary: Telecommunications in Ukraine is a rapidly evolving sector that has demonstrated resilience and growth, particularly during challenging times such as the ongoing conflict with Russia. The industry encompasses a wide range of services including mobile, fixed-line, and internet connectivity, significantly impacting the daily lives of [[ukrainians|Ukrainians]].

title: television in Ukraine
summary: Television in Ukraine has evolved significantly since its inception, beginning with experimental broadcasts in the late 1930s and developing into a diverse media landscape following the country's independence in 1991. The medium has played a crucial role in shaping public discourse and cultural identity in Ukraine.

title: Ternivka
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Ternivka is a city of regional significance located in Pavlohrad Raion, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, in eastern Ukraine, with a population of 26,961 as of 2022. It serves as the administrative center of the Ternivka urban hromada, highlighting its importance within the local governance structure of Ukraine.

title: Ternopil
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Ternopil, formerly known as Tarnopol until 1944, is a significant city in western Ukraine, situated along the Seret River. As a key urban center in the historical regions of [[galicia|Galicia]] and [[podolia|Podolia]], Ternopil plays an important role in the cultural and administrative landscape of Ukraine.

title: Ternopil Castle
summary: Ternopil Castle, known in [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] as Тернопільський замок, is a historical stronghold that played a significant role in the development of the city of Ternopil, [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. Constructed in the 16th century, the castle served to protect the southern borders of the Kingdom of Poland and the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

title: Ternopil Oblast
summary: Ternopil Oblast is a province in western Ukraine, known for its rich history, natural beauty, and cultural significance. Its administrative center is the city of Ternopil, and as of 2022, the population is estimated at 1,021,713.

title: Ternopil Raion
summary: Ternopil Raion is an administrative district located in Ternopil Oblast, [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], with its administrative center in the city of Ternopil. As of 2022, the raion has an estimated population of 559,357.

title: Ternopil Regional Art Museum
summary: The Ternopil Regional Art Museum is a significant cultural institution located in [[ternopil|Ternopil]], Ukraine, established on May 1, 1991. It serves to preserve and exhibit a diverse collection of artworks, emphasizing both Ukrainian and Western European art.

title: Tetiana Chornovol
summary: Tetiana Mykolaivna Chornovol is a prominent Ukrainian journalist and civic activist known for her role in the Euromaidan protests and her investigative work on corruption in Ukraine. She has served in the Verkhovna Rada and has actively participated in military efforts during the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.

title: The Holocaust in Ukraine
summary: The Holocaust in Ukraine refers to the systematic extermination of Jews during World War II, particularly under Nazi occupation in various regions that are now part of Ukraine. It is estimated that between 850,000 and 1,600,000 Jews were murdered, with significant local collaboration contributing to the genocide.

title: The Velveteen Rabbit
summary: The Velveteen Rabbit is a British children's book by Margery Williams, first published in 1922, that tells the story of a stuffed rabbit's longing to become real through the love of a child. Its themes of love and transformation resonate universally, including within [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] culture.

title: theatre in Ukraine
summary: Ukrainian theatre, known as Театральне мистецтво України, is a significant form of cultural expression that utilizes live performances to reflect the traditions, language, and [[culture-of-ukraine|culture of Ukraine]]. The history of Ukrainian theatre dates back to the early 17th century, evolving through various historical periods and influences.

title: tourism in Ukraine
summary: Tourism in Ukraine has historically attracted over 20 million foreign visitors annually before the 2014 Russian annexation of Crimea, which significantly reduced these numbers. The country offers diverse attractions ranging from natural landscapes to historical sites, contributing to its economy despite being underdeveloped.

title: Transcarpathia
summary: Transcarpathia is a historical region primarily located in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]]'s [[zakarpattia-oblast|Zakarpattia Oblast]], characterized by its diverse ethnic composition and complex historical affiliations. It has been part of various states throughout history, including the Kingdom of Hungary, Czechoslovakia, and the Soviet Union, before becoming an integral part of [[independent-ukraine|independent Ukraine]].

title: Transnistria
summary: Transnistria, officially referred to as the Pridnestrovian Moldavian Republic (PMR), is a landlocked breakaway entity recognized internationally as part of Moldova. It is situated along the Dniester River and borders Ukraine, with significant implications for regional stability and ethnic relations.

title: Transnistria conflict
summary: The Transnistria conflict is an ongoing frozen conflict between Moldova and the self-proclaimed state of Transnistria, which declared independence in 1990. This conflict has significant implications for Ukraine, particularly in the context of regional stability and security, especially following the Russian [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|invasion of Ukraine]] in 2022.

title: transport in Ukraine
summary: Transport in Ukraine encompasses various modes, including road, rail, water, air, and pipelines, playing a crucial role in the nation's economy and connectivity. The transportation sector contributes approximately 11% to the country's GDP and employs around 7% of the workforce.

title: Treaty of Moscow
summary: The Treaty of Moscow, also known as the Treaty of Brotherhood, was a significant agreement signed on 16 March 1921 between the Grand National Assembly of Turkey and Soviet Russia. This treaty played a crucial role in shaping the geopolitical landscape of the region, including territories relevant to Ukraine's historical context.

title: Treaty of Pereyaslav
summary: The Treaty of Pereyaslav, signed in January 1654 in central Ukraine, marked a significant pledge of allegiance by the Zaporozhian Cossacks to the Russian Tsar Alexis I. This agreement, stemming from the Khmelnytsky Uprising, established a complex relationship between the Cossack Hetmanate and the Tsardom of Russia, influencing Ukraine's political landscape for centuries.

title: trembita
summary: The trembita is a wooden alpine horn traditionally associated with the Hutsul highlanders of [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]]. It serves both musical and signaling purposes within the cultural practices of the region.

title: Truskavets
summary: Truskavets is a city located in the Drohobych Raion of Lviv Oblast, Ukraine, renowned for its mineral springs and spa facilities. It serves as a significant health resort destination, attracting numerous visitors, primarily from Ukraine and Belarus.

title: Tysmenytsia
summary: Tysmenytsia is a small city located in the Ivano-Frankivsk Raion of [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of the Tysmenytsia urban hromada. As of 2022, its population is estimated to be 8,958.

title: UEFA Euro 2012
type: edition of the UEFA European Championship
summary: UEFA Euro 2012 was the 14th edition of the UEFA European Championship, co-hosted by Poland and Ukraine from 8 June to 1 July 2012. The tournament was notable for being the first time Ukraine hosted a major international football event, culminating in Spain's victory over Italy in the final held at the Olympic Stadium in Kyiv.

title: Ukraine
summary: Ukraine is a sovereign state located in Eastern Europe, recognized as the second-largest country in Europe. It has a rich historical legacy, marked by early human settlement, the establishment of Kievan Rus', and significant events leading to its independence in 1991.

title: Ukraine during World War I
summary: During World War I, Ukraine was divided between the Russian and Austro-Hungarian Empires, with significant implications for its population and nationalist movements. The war exacerbated existing tensions and led to widespread suffering among Ukrainians caught in the conflict.

title: Ukraine east
summary: Eastern Ukraine, known as Skhidna Ukrayina in Ukrainian, encompasses the territory of Ukraine located east of the Dnipro River, primarily including Kharkiv, Luhansk, and Donetsk oblasts. This region is significant for its dense population and urbanization, as well as its pivotal role in the ongoing conflict involving Ukraine and Russian-backed forces.

title: Ukraine International Airlines
summary: Ukraine International Airlines PJSC, commonly known as UIA, served as the flag carrier and largest airline in Ukraine, headquartered in Kyiv with its primary hub at Boryspil International Airport. The airline provided both domestic and international passenger and cargo services until its operations were severely impacted by the Russo-Ukrainian war, leading to its suspension and subsequent bankruptcy in 2023.

title: Ukraine men's national football team
summary: The Ukraine men's national football team represents Ukraine in international men's football and is governed by the Ukrainian Association of Football. Established after Ukraine's independence, the team has achieved significant milestones in international competitions, including reaching the quarter-finals of the FIFA World Cup and UEFA European Championship.
aliases: Ukraine men's national association football team

title: Ukraine women's national football team
summary: The Ukraine women's national football team represents Ukraine in international women's football and is governed by the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] Association of Football. Established on 30 June 1992, the team has participated in various international competitions, including the UEFA Women's Euro 2009.

title: Ukraine-NATO relations
summary: Ukraine-NATO relations have evolved significantly since Ukraine's independence in 1991, marked by a series of cooperative agreements and increasing aspirations for NATO membership, particularly following Russian aggression in 2014 and 2022.

title: Ukraine–European Union relations
summary: Ukraine–European Union relations are defined by the Ukraine–European Union Association Agreement and the Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area (DCFTA), highlighting Ukraine's strategic partnership with the EU. The relationship has evolved significantly, culminating [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] being granted candidate status for EU accession in June 2022.

title: Ukrainian
summary: Ukrainian is an East Slavic language predominantly spoken in Ukraine, serving as the native language for a significant majority of its population. The language has evolved through various historical phases, influenced by neighboring languages and cultures, and is characterized by its unique phonetic and grammatical features.

title: Ukrainian Americans
summary: Ukrainian Americans are individuals in the United States with full or partial Ukrainian ancestry, numbering over 1 million as of 2018. They represent the second largest Ukrainian population outside the former Eastern Bloc, with significant communities in major metropolitan areas.

title: Ukrainian architecture
summary: Ukrainian architecture reflects a rich history influenced by various cultures and styles, originating from the Eastern Slavic state of Kievan Rus' and evolving through significant historical periods. The architectural landscape of Ukraine showcases a blend of Byzantine, Gothic, Renaissance, Baroque, and modern influences, marking its unique identity within the broader context of Eastern European architecture.

title: Ukrainian avant-garde
summary: The Ukrainian avant-garde represents a significant art movement in Ukraine from the late 1890s to the mid-1930s, encompassing various forms of artistic expression including painting, sculpture, literature, and theater. This movement is closely associated with notable Ukrainian artists and cities, reflecting the cultural and historical context of Ukraine during this period.

title: Ukrainian Baroque
summary: Ukrainian Baroque, also referred to as Cossack Baroque or Mazepa Baroque, is an artistic style that flourished in Ukraine during the 17th and 18th centuries, characterized by a blend of local traditions and European Baroque influences. This style significantly shaped Ukrainian culture, giving rise to many national symbols and archetypes.

title: Ukrainian Canadian Congress
summary: The Ukrainian Canadian Congress (UCC) is a nonprofit umbrella organization representing Ukrainian-Canadian political, cultural, and religious groups, established in 1940. The UCC plays a significant role in advocating for the interests of Ukrainian Canadians and maintaining connections to Ukraine.

title: Ukrainian Carpathians
summary: The Ukrainian Carpathians are a segment of the Eastern Carpathians located in the southwestern part of Ukraine, spanning four administrative regions. This mountain range is significant for its diverse geological features and cultural relevance within Ukraine.

title: Ukrainian Civil War
summary: The term 'Ukrainian Civil War' encompasses several significant conflicts in Ukraine's history, primarily during the early 20th century. These conflicts played a crucial role in shaping Ukraine's national identity and political landscape.

title: Ukrainian Communist Party
summary: The Ukrainian Communist Party (Ukrainian: Українська комуністична партія) was an oppositional political entity in Soviet Ukraine, active from 1920 until 1925, primarily composed of former members of the Ukrainian Social Democratic Labour Party. Known as Ukapists, the party sought to promote Ukrainian interests within the socialist framework of the time.

title: Ukrainian Contemporary Art
summary: Ukrainian contemporary art represents a diverse array of artistic practices that have evolved in Ukraine from the late Soviet era to the present, influenced by historical events such as the collapse of [[soviet-union|the Soviet Union]], the establishment of an [[independent-ukraine|independent Ukraine]], and ongoing conflicts. This art form encompasses various media including painting, sculpture, installation, performance, and socially engaged art, reflecting the social and political realities of the nation.

title: Ukrainian cuisine
summary: Ukrainian cuisine encompasses the diverse culinary traditions of Ukraine, influenced by its fertile soil and historical agricultural practices. It features a range of traditional dishes, with red borscht recognized as the national dish, and reflects the country's cultural heritage and regional similarities within Eastern European cuisine.

title: Ukrainian Cultural Foundation
summary: The Ukrainian Cultural Foundation (UCF) is a state agency established in 2017 to foster the development of national culture and art [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]. It aims to enhance access to cultural heritage, support cultural diversity, and integrate [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] culture into the global context.

title: Ukrainian Defense Industry
summary: The Ukrainian Defense Industry, known as Ukroboronprom, is the largest arms manufacturer [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] and ranks among the top 50 companies in the global arms sector. Established in 2010, it has adapted its operations in response to the ongoing conflict with Russia, including relocating parts of its production abroad since the 2022 invasion.

title: Ukrainian Democratic Party
summary: The Ukrainian Democratic Party (UDP) was a [[political-party-in-ukraine|political party in Ukraine]] that emerged in Kyiv in 1897, evolving from the General Ukrainian Nonpartisan Democratic Organization. It played a significant role in advocating for Ukrainian autonomy and parliamentary democracy during the early 20th century.

title: Ukrainian diaspora
summary: The Ukrainian diaspora consists of Ukrainians and their descendants living outside [[ukraine|Ukraine]], who often maintain connections to their ancestral homeland and a sense of Ukrainian national identity. This diaspora is widespread, particularly in post-Soviet states, North America, and parts of Europe and South America.

title: Ukrainian Dramatic Theatre of Maria Zankovetska
summary: The Ukrainian Dramatic Theatre of Maria Zankovetska, located in Lviv, Ukraine, is a historical drama theatre with roots dating back to the mid-19th century. Originally established as the Skarbek Theatre, it has undergone various transformations and remains a significant cultural institution [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

title: Ukrainian embroidery
summary: Ukrainian embroidery, known as vyshyvka, is a significant aspect of Ukraine's decorative arts, deeply rooted in the country's cultural heritage. This textile art form has evolved over centuries, featuring diverse regional styles and playing a vital role in traditional Ukrainian customs and ceremonies.

title: Ukrainian Exchange
summary: The Ukrainian Exchange, established on 15 May 2008, is a prominent stock exchange located in Kyiv, Ukraine. It has served as a key trading platform for equities and derivatives within the country, operating under the jurisdiction of the [[ministry-of-finance-of-ukraine|Ministry of Finance of Ukraine]].

title: Ukrainian folk music
summary: Ukrainian folk music encompasses various forms of traditional, folkloric, and folk-inspired popular music, as well as European classical music traditions. It has played a significant role in the cultural identity of Ukraine, particularly through its vocal and instrumental practices.

title: Ukrainian folklore
summary: Ukrainian folklore encompasses the rich folk traditions that have emerged in Ukraine and among ethnic [[ukrainians|Ukrainians]], rooted in ancient Slavic mythology and evolving into a distinct cultural identity. This folklore serves as a vital means of preserving cultural uniqueness amid external influences.

title: Ukrainian grammar
summary: Ukrainian grammar is a complex system characterized by significant inflection and a relatively flexible word order, primarily following a subject-verb-object structure. It encompasses phonological, morphological, and syntactic rules that are essential for understanding the Ukrainian language.

title: Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church
summary: The Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church (UGCC) is an autonomous Eastern Catholic church based [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], in full communion with the Holy See. It traces its origins to the Christianization of [[kievan-rus|Kievan Rus]]' in 988 and has played a significant role in the development of Ukrainian identity and culture.
aliases: Ukrainian Catholic Church of the Byzantine Tradition

title: Ukrainian Ground Forces
summary: The Ukrainian Ground Forces, also known as the Ukrainian Army, is the land force component of the [[armed-forces-of-ukraine|Armed Forces of Ukraine]]. Established from Soviet military units following Ukraine's independence, it has undergone significant modernization and expansion, particularly in response to ongoing conflicts in the region.

title: Ukrainian historical regions
summary: The historical regions of Ukraine encompass various geographic, cultural, and historical identities that have shaped the nation's development. These regions reflect Ukraine's diverse heritage and the evolution of its territorial divisions over time.

title: Ukrainian historiography
summary: Ukrainian historiography encompasses the academic study of Ukraine's history, significantly shaped by its interactions with Russia and the contributions of Ukrainian immigrant historians, particularly in Canada. This field has evolved through various interpretations and schools of thought, reflecting Ukraine's complex past and national identity.

title: Ukrainian independence referendum
summary: The Ukrainian independence referendum, held on 1 December 1991, was a pivotal event in Ukraine's history, marking the nation's formal declaration of independence from the Soviet Union. An overwhelming 92% of voters supported the declaration, which was a response to the failed August coup and the absence of a signed New Union Treaty.

title: Ukrainian Institute
summary: The Ukrainian Institute is a public institution established in 2017 to promote Ukrainian culture globally and facilitate cultural diplomacy. It operates under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine and began its activities in 2018.

title: Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance
summary: The Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance (UINM) is a central executive body under the [[cabinet-of-ministers-of-ukraine|Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine]], established to promote and preserve the national memory of the Ukrainian people. It plays a significant role in shaping memorial policy and managing the archives related to historical repression [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

title: Ukrainian Insurgent Army
summary: The Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) was a nationalist military formation established on 14 October 1942 by the Banderite faction of the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists. It played a significant role [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s struggle for independence during World War II, engaging in guerrilla warfare against both Soviet and Nazi forces until the 1950s.

title: Ukrainian literature
summary: Ukrainian literature encompasses literary works written in the Ukrainian language and those created within the territory of Ukraine, reflecting the country's historical and cultural context. Its development has been shaped significantly by foreign dominations and the evolution of the Ukrainian language as a medium for literary expression.

title: Ukrainian Museum
summary: The Ukrainian Museum, established in 1976 by the Ukrainian National Women's League of America in New York City, is the largest museum dedicated to Ukrainian art and culture outside of Ukraine. It aims to promote the understanding and preservation of Ukraine's artistic heritage through its diverse collections and exhibitions.

title: Ukrainian National Assembly – Ukrainian National Self Defence
summary: The Ukrainian National Assembly – Ukrainian People's Self-Defence (UNA-UNSO) is a Ukrainian nationalist organization comprising a political wing and a paramilitary wing. Established in 1991, it has played a significant role in far-right politics in Ukraine and has participated in various international conflicts.
aliases: Українська Національна Асамблея — Українська Народна Самооборона

title: Ukrainian National Museum
summary: The Ukrainian National Museum (UNM) is situated in the Ukrainian Village neighborhood of Chicago, USA, and serves as a repository for a diverse range of Ukrainian cultural artifacts, artworks, and historical materials.

title: Ukrainian National Revival
summary: The Ukrainian National Revival was a national liberation movement that emerged in the late 18th century, during a time when Ukraine was divided among the Austrian Empire, the Kingdom of Hungary, and the Russian Empire. This movement marked the beginning of modern Ukrainian literature and was characterized by the formation of various cultural and political organizations aimed at fostering Ukrainian identity and autonomy.

title: Ukrainian National Women's League of America
summary: The Ukrainian National Women's League of America (UNWLA) is a Ukrainian-American charitable organization founded in 1925 in New York City, dedicated to supporting social welfare, culture, and education for Ukrainian communities both in Ukraine and the diaspora.

title: Ukrainian nationalism
summary: Ukrainian nationalism is a political ideology focused on the unity of [[ukrainians|Ukrainians]] as a distinct people and the promotion of the Ukrainian state. Its modern roots trace back to the mid-17th century during the Cossack uprising against Polish-Lithuanian rule, and it encompasses various cultural, ethnic, and historical elements that define Ukrainian identity.

title: Ukrainian opera
summary: Ukrainian opera is a genre that emerged in the late 19th century, blending European theatrical traditions with Ukrainian folk music. It has evolved through various historical phases, reflecting the cultural and political landscape of Ukraine.

title: Ukrainian Orthodox Church
summary: The Ukrainian Orthodox Church encompasses various Orthodox Christian entities within Ukraine and abroad, reflecting the religious diversity and historical developments of Orthodoxy in the region.

title: Ukrainian Orthodox Church (Moscow Patriarchate)
summary: The Ukrainian Orthodox Church (UOC), often referred to as the Ukrainian Orthodox Church of the Moscow Patriarchate (UOC-MP), is an Eastern Orthodox church in Ukraine that has undergone significant changes in its governance and identity, particularly in response to geopolitical events. Established in 1990, the UOC declared its independence from the Moscow Patriarchate in May 2022 amidst the backdrop of the Russian invasion of Ukraine.
aliases: Ukrainian Orthodox Church of the Moscow Patriarchate

title: Ukrainian Orthodox Church – Kyiv Patriarchate
summary: The Ukrainian Orthodox Church – Kyiv Patriarchate (UOC-KP) is an Eastern Orthodox church that emerged in Ukraine following its independence in 1991. It has undergone significant changes and conflicts, particularly regarding its status and recognition within the broader Eastern Orthodox community.
aliases: Ukrainian Orthodox Church of the Kyivan Patriarchate

title: Ukrainian parliamentary elections
summary: Ukrainian parliamentary elections are held to establish the membership of the Verkhovna Rada for a five-year term, reflecting the political landscape of [[ukraine|Ukraine]].

title: Ukrainian People's Party
summary: The Ukrainian People's Party is a centre-right [[political-party-in-ukraine|political party in Ukraine]], established in 1999 and originally known as the Ukrainian People's Movement until 2003. It has played a significant role in various electoral processes [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] and has undergone several organizational changes throughout its history.

title: Ukrainian People's Republic
summary: The Ukrainian People's Republic (UPR) was a historical state in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]] that emerged during a period of national awakening [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]] following the February Revolution of 1917. It declared independence from Russia on 22 January 1918, amidst a backdrop of conflict involving various factions during the Ukrainian War of Independence.

title: Ukrainian presidential election
summary: Ukrainian presidential elections are held to elect the President of Ukraine for a five-year term. Since the inception of the presidency in 1991, there have been seven elections, with the next scheduled for 2024 postponed due to the ongoing Russian invasion and martial law.

title: Ukrainian Railways
summary: Ukrainian Railways, officially known as Public JSC Ukrainian Railways or PAT 'Ukrzaliznytsia (UZ)', is a state-owned company responsible for managing railway infrastructure and transportation in Ukraine. It is a significant player in the global rail transport sector, ranking as the sixth largest passenger transporter and seventh largest freight transporter worldwide.

title: Ukrainian Red Cross Society
type: National Red Cross and Red Crescent society
summary: The Ukrainian Red Cross Society is a non-profit humanitarian organization based [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], engaged in various humanitarian efforts including disaster management, health care, and support for vulnerable populations. It has been a member of the International Federation of Red Cross/Red Crescent Societies since 1993.

title: Ukrainian rock
summary: Ukrainian rock is a music genre originating from Ukraine, evolving from the VIA music scene of the 1970s and 1980s. It has played a significant role in the cultural identity and resistance movements within the country.

title: Ukrainian Socialist Party
summary: The Ukrainian Socialist Party refers to several political entities from the 20th century, each contributing to the political landscape of Ukraine. Notably, it includes parties established in 1900 and 1950, as well as the Socialist Party of Ukraine founded in 1991.

title: Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic
summary: The Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic (Ukrainian SSR) was a key constituent republic of the Soviet Union from 1922 until 1991, playing a significant role [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s historical and political landscape. Governed by the Communist Party of the Soviet Union through its Ukrainian branch, the republic underwent numerous territorial and political changes during its existence.

title: Ukrainian State
summary: The Ukrainian State (Ukrainian: Українська Держава) was the official designation for Ukraine from April 29 to December 14, 1918. Under the autocratic rule of Hetman Pavlo Skoropadsky, the state represented a significant period in [[history-of-ukraine|Ukrainian history]] marked by political dependency on the Central Powers and internal dissent.

title: Ukrainian State Film Agency
summary: The Ukrainian State Film Agency, known as Derzhkino, is the principal executive body overseeing cinematography in Ukraine, established in 2011 to implement state policy in the film sector.

title: Ukrainian traditional costumes
summary: Ukrainian traditional costumes reflect the rich cultural heritage of ethnic Ukrainians, characterized by distinct garments such as the vyshyvanka, sashes, and vinok flower crowns. The clothing styles vary across the four macroregions of Ukraine, showcasing differences in gender, social status, and local influences.

title: Ukrainian War of Independence
summary: The Ukrainian War of Independence, also known as the [[ukrainiansoviet-war|Ukrainian–Soviet War]], occurred from March 1917 to November 1921, forming a significant part of the Russian Civil War and leading to the establishment of an independent Ukrainian republic. This conflict involved various factions vying for control over Ukraine, ultimately resulting in the incorporation of much of the territory into the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic.

title: Ukrainian wine
summary: The wine [[industry-in-ukraine|industry in Ukraine]] has a rich history and is characterized by its unique geographical regions, particularly near the Black Sea and in Zakarpattia Oblast. Despite challenges, including the ongoing conflict and the loss of significant vineyard areas, [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] winemakers have continued to produce and export their wines.

title: Ukrainian Women's Union
summary: The Ukrainian Women's Union (Ukrainian: Союз українок) was a prominent women's organization that operated from 1920 to 1938, primarily among Ukrainian women outside of [[ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic|Soviet Ukraine]], advocating for both gender recognition and nationalist aims.

title: Ukrainian World Congress
summary: The Ukrainian World Congress (UWC) is a non-profit, nonpartisan international organization that coordinates Ukrainian public organizations in the diaspora. Founded in 1967 and renamed in 1993, the UWC advocates for the interests of Ukrainians globally and supports Ukraine's sovereignty and cultural identity.

title: Ukrainians
summary: Ukrainians are an East Slavic ethnic group primarily associated with Ukraine, where they constitute over three-quarters of the population. With a global population of approximately 46 million, they are the second largest Slavic ethnic group after Russians.

title: Ukrainians in Italy
summary: Ukrainians in Italy primarily consist of recent labor migrants, with a significant presence in the caregiving sector. As of 2020, there were 223,000 Ukrainians in Italy, making them the fourth-largest immigrant group in the country.

title: Ukrainians in Poland
summary: Ukrainians in Poland represent a significant ethnic group with various legal statuses, including ethnic minority, residents, and refugees. Their population has fluctuated dramatically, particularly following the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022, highlighting their deep connection to Ukraine.

title: Ukrainian–Soviet War
summary: The Ukrainian–Soviet War refers to the conflict between the Ukrainian People's Republic and the Bolshevik forces from 1917 to 1921, following the October Revolution. This war is significant in [[history-of-ukraine|Ukrainian history]] as it represents a struggle for independence amidst the backdrop of broader revolutionary and civil conflicts in the region.

title: Ukrainization
summary: Ukrainization is a policy aimed at promoting the Ukrainian language and culture across various public domains [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], as well as assimilating non-Ukrainians into Ukrainian cultural practices. This process has historical roots and has evolved through different political contexts in Ukraine.

title: Ukrainska Pravda
summary: Ukrainska Pravda is a prominent Ukrainian socio-political online media outlet, established in April 2000 by Heorhii Gongadze. It has played a significant role in advocating for press freedom and has been influential in various political movements in Ukraine.

title: Ukrnafta
summary: Public JSC Ukrnafta is the largest oil and natural gas extraction company in Ukraine, also managing a significant network of gas filling stations. Established in 1994, it plays a crucial role in the country's energy sector and has undergone significant changes in governance and ownership.

title: Uman
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Uman is a city of regional significance located in [[cherkasy-oblast|Cherkasy Oblast]], central Ukraine, known for its historical importance and cultural heritage. It serves as an administrative center and is recognized for its role in [[ukrainian-literature|Ukrainian literature]] and as a pilgrimage site for Breslov Hasidic Jews.

title: Uzh River
summary: The Uzh River is a significant waterway located in western Ukraine and eastern Slovakia, originating in the [[ukrainian-carpathians|Ukrainian Carpathians]] and flowing through the city of Uzhhorod before joining the Laborec River. It plays an important role in the geography, ecology, and economy of the Zakarpattia Oblast [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

title: Uzhhorod
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Uzhhorod is a city located on the Uzh River in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of [[zakarpattia-oblast|Zakarpattia Oblast]]. With a population of 115,449 as of 2022, it is notable for its geographical significance and rich historical background.

title: Uzhhorod Castle
summary: Uzhhorod Castle is a significant historical citadel located in Uzhhorod, Ukraine, known for its diverse architectural styles and rich history dating back to the 13th century. The castle played an important role in the historical narrative of Hungary and the region.

title: Uzhhorod National University
summary: Uzhhorod National University (UzhNU) is a prominent state-sponsored university located in Uzhhorod, Ukraine, founded on October 18, 1945. It is recognized for its extensive academic programs and significant contributions to education and research in the region.
aliases: State Higher Education Establishment "Uzhhorod National University"

title: varenyky
summary: Varenyky are traditional Ukrainian dumplings made from unleavened dough filled with various ingredients, making them a significant part of Ukrainian cuisine and culture.

title: VARTA AG
summary: VARTA AG is a German company specializing in the production of batteries for various markets, including automotive, industrial, and consumer sectors. Its historical developments and recent restructuring efforts have implications for its operations in Ukraine and the broader European market.

title: Vasyl Krychevsky
summary: Vasyl Hryhorovych Krychevsky was a prominent Ukrainian painter, architect, art scholar, graphic artist, and educator, recognized for his contributions to Ukrainian art and design, including the 1918 Ukrainian coat of arms and state seals.

title: Vasyl Slipak
summary: Vasyl Yaroslavovych Slipak was a prominent Ukrainian baritone opera singer, recognized for his performances in France and his contributions to [[music-of-ukraine|Ukrainian music]]. He served as a volunteer in the Ukrainian army during the [[war-in-donbas|war in Donbas]] and was posthumously honored with the title of Hero of Ukraine.

title: Vasyl Stus
summary: Vasyl Semenovych Stus (6 January 1938 – 4 September 1985) was a prominent Ukrainian poet, translator, literary critic, journalist, and a key figure in the Ukrainian dissident movement. His opposition to the Soviet regime led to his imprisonment and eventual death in a labor camp, cementing his legacy as one of Ukraine's most significant literary figures.

title: Vasyl Symonenko
summary: Vasyl Andriiovych Symonenko (8 January 1935 – 13 December 1963) was a prominent Ukrainian poet, journalist, and activist associated with the dissident movement, recognized as a key figure in early 1960s [[ukrainian-literature|Ukrainian literature]]. His works and untimely death significantly influenced the national democratic movement [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

title: Vasylivka
summary: Vasylivka is a city located in the [[zaporizhzhia-oblast|Zaporizhzhia Oblast]] of southern Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Vasylivka Raion. As of 2022, the population is estimated at 12,567, and the city is situated on the banks of the Kakhovka Reservoir on the Dnieper River.

title: Velykyi Bychkiv
summary: Velykyi Bychkiv is a rural settlement located in the Rakhiv Raion of [[zakarpattia-oblast|Zakarpattia Oblast]], [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. As of 2022, it has an estimated population of 9,114 and is part of the Velykyi Bychkiv settlement hromada.

title: Verkhovna Rada
summary: The Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine serves as the unicameral parliament of the nation, consisting of 450 deputies and located in Kyiv. It has evolved from historical legislative bodies and plays a crucial role in shaping Ukraine's laws and policies.

title: Vernadsky National Library of Ukraine
summary: The Vernadsky National Library of Ukraine (VNLU) serves as the primary academic library and scientific information center [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], recognized as one of the largest national libraries globally. Established in 1918, it is located in Kyiv and houses approximately 15 million items, including significant collections of Slavic writings and archives related to Ukrainian scientists and cultural figures.

title: Viktor Medvedchuk
summary: Viktor Volodymyrovych Medvedchuk is a former Ukrainian lawyer, business oligarch, and politician known for his pro-Kremlin stance and close ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin. He has been a significant figure in Ukrainian politics, particularly in relation to the country's geopolitical orientation and internal conflicts.

title: Viktor Tikhonov
summary: Viktor Tikhonov is a name associated with multiple notable individuals, particularly in the context of Ukrainian politics and sports.

title: Viktor Tsoi
summary: Viktor Tsoi was a prominent Soviet singer-songwriter and actor, co-founder of the influential band Kino, which played a significant role in the development of rock music in the Soviet Union. His work resonated with youth across the region, including Ukraine, particularly during the transformative period of Perestroika.

title: Viktor Yanukovych
summary: Viktor Fedorovych Yanukovych, born on 9 July 1950, is a former Ukrainian politician who served as the fourth [[president-of-ukraine|president of Ukraine]] from 2010 to 2014. His political career was marked by significant events including the 2014 [[revolution-of-dignity|Revolution of Dignity]], which led to his removal from office and subsequent exile in Russia.

title: Viktor Yushchenko
summary: Viktor Andriiovych Yushchenko is a prominent Ukrainian politician who served as the third president of Ukraine from 23 January 2005 to 25 February 2010, known for his pro-Western orientation and leadership during pivotal moments in Ukraine's political history.

title: Vinnytsia
summary: Vinnytsia is a city in west-central Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Vinnytsia Oblast and Vinnytsia Raion. With a population of 431,319 as of July 2026, it is the largest city in the historic region of [[podolia|Podillia]] and has a rich history dating back to the Middle Ages.

title: Vinnytsia Oblast
summary: Vinnytsia Oblast is an administrative region in central Ukraine, with its capital in the city of Vinnytsia. As of 2022, it has a population of approximately 1.5 million residents and is rich in historical, geographical, and economic significance.

title: Vira Vovk
summary: Vira Ostapivna Selianska, known by her pen name Vira Vovk, was a prominent Ukrainian writer, critic, and translator, born on 2 January 1926 in Boryslav and passing away on 16 July 2022 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Her literary contributions and advocacy for Ukrainian culture have had a significant impact, particularly in the diaspora.

title: Vistula
summary: The Vistula is the longest river in Poland and the primary river draining into the Baltic Sea, measuring 1,047 kilometers (651 miles) in length. Its significance extends beyond Poland, impacting neighboring countries and playing a vital role in the cultural and historical identity of the region, including [[ukraine|Ukraine]].

title: visual arts of Ukraine
summary: Visual arts of Ukraine encompass the historical and cultural artistic expressions from the regions that constitute [[modern-history-of-ukraine|modern Ukraine]]. The evolution of these arts reflects a rich tapestry of traditions influenced by various cultures throughout history.

title: Vitali Klitschko
summary: Vitali Klitschko is a prominent Ukrainian politician and former professional boxer, serving as the mayor of Kyiv since 2014. He is recognized for his significant contributions to both sports and politics in Ukraine, particularly during the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

title: Vladimir Lenin
summary: Vladimir Lenin, born Vladimir Ilyich Ulyanov, was a significant Russian revolutionary and political theorist who played a crucial role in the establishment of Soviet governance. His actions and ideologies had a profound impact on Ukraine, particularly during the tumultuous events surrounding the Russian Revolution and the subsequent formation of the Soviet Union.

title: Vladimir Putin
summary: Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin, born on 7 October 1952, is a prominent Russian politician and former intelligence officer who has held the presidency of Russia since 2012, with a previous term from 2000 to 2008. His actions and policies have significantly impacted Ukraine, particularly through military interventions and territorial annexations.

title: Vladimir Shcherbakov
summary: Vladimir Shcherbakov refers to several notable individuals, primarily associated with the Soviet Union, including politicians, a general, and a footballer, each of whom has connections to Ukraine's historical and political landscape.

title: Vladimir the Great
summary: Vladimir I Sviatoslavich, also known as Volodymyr I Sviatoslavych and referred to as 'the Great', was a significant historical figure who served as Prince of Novgorod and Grand Prince of Kiev, playing a crucial role in the Christianization of Kievan Rus'. He is recognized as a saint in both the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox Churches.

title: Volhynia
summary: Volhynia, a historic region in Central and [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]], is primarily located in northwestern Ukraine and has significant historical and cultural relevance to the country. It encompasses parts of several Ukrainian oblasts, including Volyn, [[rivne|Rivne]], and portions of [[zhytomyr|Zhytomyr]], [[ternopil|Ternopil]], and [[khmelnytskyi|Khmelnytskyi]] Oblasts.

title: Volodymyr Hroisman
summary: Volodymyr Hroisman is a prominent [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] politician and businessman who held the position of Prime Minister of Ukraine from 2016 to 2019. His political career has been marked by significant contributions to local governance and national reforms, particularly in decentralization and public administration.

title: Volodymyr Viatrovych
summary: Volodymyr Mykhailovych Viatrovych is a Ukrainian historian, civic activist, and politician, known for his roles in national remembrance and historical research related to Ukraine's liberation movements. He served as the Director of the Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance and has been a member of the [[verkhovna-rada|Ukrainian parliament]] since December 2019.

title: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
summary: Volodymyr Oleksandrovych Zelenskyy is a prominent Ukrainian politician and former entertainer, serving as the sixth [[president-of-ukraine|president of Ukraine]] since 2019. His presidency has been marked by significant challenges, including the ongoing Russo-Ukrainian war and efforts to unify the country's diverse population.

title: Volyn Oblast
summary: Volyn Oblast, located in northwestern Ukraine, is a province bordered by Rivne Oblast, Lviv Oblast, Poland, and Belarus. Its administrative center is Lutsk, and as of 2022, it has a population of 1,021,356.

title: Vorkuta Gulag
summary: The Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp, commonly referred to as Vorkutlag, was a significant Gulag labor camp in the Soviet Union, operational from 1932 until 1962. It is notable for its connection to [[ukraine|Ukraine]], particularly during World War II when it became a vital source of coal following the occupation of [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] coal-producing regions.

title: Vorskla
summary: The Vorskla is a significant river in northeastern Ukraine, originating from Belgorod Oblast in Russia and flowing into the Dnieper. It is notable for its length and the cities it traverses, as well as its historical importance.

title: Vostok Battalion
summary: Vostok Battalion refers to a Russian militant group that has operated in the Donbas region of Ukraine and was later integrated into the Russian Armed Forces. It is also associated with former Spetsnaz units of the Russian military intelligence based in Chechnya.

title: Vuhledar
summary: Vuhledar is a city located in Volnovakha Raion, Donetsk Oblast, eastern [[ukraine|Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of the Vuhledar urban hromada. Established during the 1960s coal industry development, it has a population of 14,144 as of early 2022 and has been significantly impacted by the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.

title: Vynnyky
summary: Vynnyky is a small city located in Lviv Raion of Lviv Oblast, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], with a population of approximately 19,037 as of 2022. The city has a rich historical background and is part of the Lviv urban hromada.

title: vyshyvanka
summary: Vyshyvanka refers to the embroidered shirt integral to Ukrainian and Belarusian national costumes, characterized by unique regional embroidery styles. This garment serves not only as traditional attire but also as a symbol of cultural identity and patriotism in Ukraine.

title: War in Donbas
summary: The war in Donbas, a significant phase of the Russo-Ukrainian war, erupted in April 2014 in the eastern region of Ukraine, marked by a conflict between Russian-backed paramilitaries and the Ukrainian government. This conflict led to the establishment of self-proclaimed republics and continued until it was overshadowed by the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

title: West Ukrainian National University
summary: West Ukrainian National University (WUNU) is a state-sponsored institution established in 1966 in Ternopil, [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. It is recognized as one of the leading public universities in the region and has notable alumni, including former [[president-of-ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[viktor-yushchenko|Viktor Yushchenko]].

title: West Ukrainian People's Republic
summary: The West Ukrainian People's Republic (ZUNR) was a short-lived state that existed from November 1918 to July 1919, primarily in the region of Galicia. It emerged during the disintegration of Austria-Hungary and sought to establish Ukrainian autonomy amid competing claims from Poland.

title: Western Bug
summary: The Western Bug is a significant river in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]], flowing through Ukraine, Poland, and Belarus, with a total length of 774 kilometres (481 mi). It serves as a natural border between Ukraine and Poland for 185 kilometres (115 mi) and is connected to the [[dnieper|Dnieper River]] through the Dnieper–Bug Canal.

title: Western Ukraine
summary: Western Ukraine, known as Zakhidna Ukrayina in Ukrainian, encompasses the western territories of Ukraine, including several contemporary administrative regions. Historically significant, this region has been shaped by various political entities and cultural influences, making it a vital part of Ukraine's national identity.

title: Witold Pilecki
summary: Witold Pilecki was a Polish cavalry officer, intelligence agent, and resistance leader during World War II, known for his infiltration of Auschwitz and his efforts to document Nazi atrocities. His life and actions are significant in the context of both Polish and Ukrainian history during the war.

title: Women in Ukraine
summary: Women in Ukraine possess equal constitutional rights to men across various sectors, including economic, political, cultural, and social realms. Despite this legal equality, women face significant challenges, particularly in instances of violence and underrepresentation in leadership roles.

title: Yalta
summary: Yalta is a resort city located on the southern coast of the [[crimea|Crimean Peninsula]], recognized internationally as part of [[ukraine|Ukraine]] and serving as the administrative center of Yalta Municipality. Despite its official status, Yalta has been under de facto Russian control since the [[russian-annexation-of-crimea|annexation of Crimea]] in 2014.

title: Yalta Conference
summary: The Yalta Conference, held from February 4 to 11, 1945, was a pivotal meeting of the leaders of the United States, the United Kingdom, and the Soviet Union to discuss the postwar reorganization of Europe, including issues directly impacting Ukraine. The conference took place in [[crimean-khanate|Crimea]] and set the stage for the political landscape of Eastern Europe after World War II.

title: Yaremche
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Yaremche is a town of regional significance located in Nadvirna Raion, Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast, Ukraine. Situated at an altitude of approximately 580 meters above sea level, it serves as the administrative center of the Yaremche urban hromada and has a population of 7,907 as of 2022.

title: Yavoriv
summary: Yavoriv is a city located in Lviv Oblast, [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], approximately 15 kilometers from the Polish border. It serves as the administrative center of Yavoriv Raion and has a population of approximately 12,785 as of 2022.

title: Yelena Gagarina
summary: Yelena Yurievna Gagarina is a Russian art historian and the general director of Moscow Kremlin Museums since 2001. She is notably recognized as the daughter of Yuri Gagarin, the first human in space, and has connections to significant cultural and political events related to Ukraine.

title: Yevgeny Prigozhin
summary: Yevgeny Viktorovich Prigozhin (1 June 1961 – 23 August 2023) was a Russian mercenary leader and oligarch known for his leadership of the Wagner Group, a private military company involved in the conflict in Ukraine. He was a significant figure in the Russian military operations and political landscape, particularly regarding Russia's actions in Ukraine and his connections to the Kremlin.

title: Yevhen Hutsalo
summary: Yevhen Hutsalo was a prominent Ukrainian writer and journalist known for his contributions to literature and his engagement with the socio-political landscape of Ukraine during the 20th century.

title: Yevhen Konoplyanka
summary: Yevhen Olehovych Konoplyanka is a retired Ukrainian professional footballer known for his role as a winger. He had a significant impact on Ukrainian football, representing the national team and achieving success at club level both domestically and internationally.

title: Yevhen Konovalets
summary: Yevhen Mykhailovych Konovalets was a prominent Ukrainian military commander and political leader, instrumental in the Ukrainian nationalist movement during the early 20th century. He is recognized for his leadership in the Ukrainian War of Independence and as the founding leader of the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN).

title: Yevhen Stankovych
summary: Yevhen Fedorovych Stankovych is a prominent contemporary Ukrainian composer known for his diverse works in stage, orchestral, chamber, and choral music.

title: Yevpatoriya
summary: Yevpatoriya is a city located in western Crimea, north of Kalamita Bay, serving as the administrative center of Yevpatoria Municipality. As of the 2014 Census, it had a population of 105,719 and is recognized for its historical significance and contemporary role as a resort town within the context of [[ukraine|Ukraine]].

title: Yulia Tymoshenko
summary: Yulia Volodymyrivna Tymoshenko is a prominent Ukrainian politician who served as the first female [[prime-minister-of-ukraine|Prime Minister of Ukraine]], holding office in 2005 and again from 2007 to 2010. She is known for her leadership in the Batkivshchyna political party and her significant role in Ukraine's political landscape, including her involvement in the Orange Revolution and various presidential elections.

title: Zakarpattia
summary: Zakarpattia refers to various entities associated with the region of Zakarpattia Oblast [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], including its administrative structure, historical context, and cultural significance.

title: Zakarpattia Oblast
summary: Zakarpattia Oblast is an administrative region in western Ukraine, situated in the Carpathian Mountains and historically known as Carpathian Ruthenia. It was established on January 22, 1946, and serves as a significant cultural and economic area, characterized by its diverse population and tourism industry.

title: Zaliznyi Port
summary: Zaliznyi Port is a resort village located along the Black Sea coast in Kherson Oblast, Ukraine. Known for its historical significance and recent challenges during the [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|Russo-Ukrainian war]], it serves as a notable example of the region's cultural and geopolitical dynamics.

title: Zaporizhian Sich
summary: The Zaporozhian Sich was a semi-autonomous polity and proto-state of the Zaporozhian Cossacks, existing from the 16th to the 18th centuries, primarily in southeastern Ukraine. It played a significant role in the defense of Ukrainian territories against external threats while also being a center of Cossack life and governance.

title: Zaporizhzhia
summary: Zaporizhzhia is a significant city in southeast Ukraine, located on the banks of the Dnieper River and serving as the administrative center of [[zaporizhzhia-oblast|Zaporizhzhia Oblast]]. With a population of 710,052 as of 2022, it is known for its industrial capabilities, historical significance, and the island of Khortytsia.

title: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant
summary: The Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, located in southeastern Ukraine, is the largest nuclear power facility in Europe and ranks among the top ten globally. Since 2022, it has been under Russian control, significantly impacting Ukraine's energy landscape.

title: Zaporizhzhia Oblast
summary: Zaporizhzhia Oblast is a region located in south-[[ukraine-east|east Ukraine]], with its administrative center in the city of Zaporizhzhia. Covering an area of 27,183 square kilometers and having a population of approximately 1,638,462 as of 2022, the oblast plays a significant role [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s industrial and agricultural sectors.

title: Zaporozhian Cossacks
summary: The Zaporozhian Cossacks, also referred to as the Zaporozhian Cossack Army or Zaporozhian Host, were a significant group of Cossacks [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], primarily composed of [[rusyns|Ruthenians]] and other ethnicities, who established a notable military and political presence from the 15th to the 18th century.

title: Zavodske
summary: Zavodske is a city located in Myrhorod Raion, Poltava Oblast, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of the Zavodske urban hromada. As of 2022, the city has a population of 7,712 and is situated in the forest steppe zone of the Dnieper lowland.

title: Zbarazh Castle
summary: Zbarazh Castle is a fortified stronghold located in Zbarazh, [[ternopil-oblast|Ternopil Oblast]], Ukraine, built during the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth period. It has historical significance as a military and aristocratic site, associated with notable families such as the Zbaraski and Wiśniowiecki families.

title: Zboriv
summary: Zboriv is a small city located in [[ternopil-raion|Ternopil Raion]], Ternopil Oblast, in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], within the historical region of [[galicia|Galicia]]. As of 2022, it has an estimated population of 6,621 and serves as the administrative center of Zboriv urban hromada.

title: Zbruch
